people.name: Achan
people.description: Israelite who took forbidden plunder from Jericho; caused defeat at Ai.
people.dateNotes: Josh 7:1-26. Ussher, Annals §313: 1451 BC (AM 2553c).

people.name: Salmon
people.description: Son of Nahshon; husband of Rahab according to Matthew. Father of Boaz. Ancestor of David and Jesus.
people.dateNotes: Ruth 4:20-21; Matt 1:4-5; 1 Chr 2:11. Life dates estimated; Matthew makes him the husband of Rahab of Jericho (1451 BC). The line Salmon, Boaz, Obed, Jesse, David spans roughly 1450 to 1085 BC, too long for four generations, so the genealogy is generally taken to be abbreviated, as Hebrew genealogies often are.

people.name: Phinehas
people.description: Zealous priest who stopped a plague by his decisive action.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. A grown man when he killed Zimri at Baal-peor in 1452 BC (Num 25:7-13); still ministering before the ark in the Benjamite war (Judg 20:28), which Ussher places after the death of Joshua's elders, before c. 1413 BC.

events.role: Priest who ended the plague at Baal-peor (Num 25)

people.name: Rahab
people.description: A woman of Jericho who hid Israel's spies and confessed their God as Lord of heaven and earth, securing her family's rescue by a scarlet cord. Grafted into Israel, she appears in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus and is praised for her faith in both Hebrews and James.
people.dateNotes: Josh 2; 6:22-25; Matt 1:5; Heb 11:31. Life dates estimated; an adult at the fall of Jericho in 1451 BC.

people.name: Achsah
people.description: Daughter of Caleb, offered in marriage to whoever would take Kirjath-sepher. Othniel took the city and married her, and she then asked her father for springs of water to go with her southern land.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Married when Caleb was about eighty-five (Josh 14:10; 15:16-19), so born in the 1470s BC. Scripture gives no dates for her.

scripture.context: Given to Othniel after Kirjath-sepher is taken

people.name: Othniel
people.description: First judge of Israel: Othniel son of Kenaz, "Caleb's younger brother" (Judg 3:9), of Judah, who took Kirjath-sepher and married Caleb's daughter Achsah. The Spirit of the LORD came upon him and he delivered Israel from Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia (Judg 3:8-11).
people.dateNotes: Took Kirjath-sepher (Debir) in Joshua's lifetime, which Ussher dates 1446 BC (Annals §328; Josh 15:16-17; Judg 1:11-13), so born by about 1470 BC. Delivered Israel 1405 BC (Annals §342; the eight years of Cushan began 1413, §341) after eight years of oppression by Cushan-rishathaim (Judg 3:8-10). Ussher measures each period of rest (Judg 3:11, 3:30, 5:31, 8:28) from the previous deliverance, so the figure includes the oppression that he ended. Birth and death are estimates; Judg 3:11 records his death without a year. The texts call Othniel the son of Kenaz and Caleb's (younger) brother; since Caleb is the son of Jephunneh (Num 13:6), the wording is ambiguous and no sibling link is recorded.

scripture.context: Son of Kenaz; father of Hathath

people.name: Gera, father of Ehud
people.description: Benjamite, father of Ehud, the left-handed judge who killed Eglon, king of Moab.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Ehud (born 1365 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him. Other men of the same name appear in Benjamin's genealogies.

scripture.context: Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite

people.name: Ehud
people.description: Left-handed Benjamite judge, son of Gera, who killed Eglon king of Moab with a hidden dagger and then led Israel to subdue Moab (Judg 3:15-30).
people.dateNotes: Moab oppressed Israel eighteen years (Judg 3:14), c. 1343-1325 BC; Ehud killed Eglon c. 1325 BC (Ussher), who counts the eighty years of rest (Judg 3:30) from Othniel's deliverance. Israel sinned again "when Ehud was dead" (Judg 4:1), before Jabin's oppression began c. 1305 BC. Birth and death are estimates.

scripture.context: Father of Naaman, Ahiah and Gera

people.name: Abinoam
people.description: Father of Barak, who led Israel's army with Deborah against Sisera. He was from Kedesh in Naphtali.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Barak (born 1320 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Barak the son of Abinoam of Kedesh-naphtali

people.name: Shamgar
people.description: Son of Anath, named after Ehud as one who "also delivered Israel", killing six hundred Philistines with an ox goad (Judg 3:31). The Song of Deborah recalls "the days of Shamgar" as a time when the highways were deserted (Judg 5:6).
people.dateNotes: No years are given. Ussher places him after Ehud (c. 1325 BC), and Judg 5:6 makes him an older contemporary of Deborah and Jael (c. 1285 BC). Life dates are estimates.

scripture.context: Shamgar delivers Israel with an ox goad

people.name: Joash, father of Gideon
people.description: Abiezrite of Ophrah, father of Gideon. He kept an altar to Baal that Gideon tore down, and defended his son when the townsmen demanded his death.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Gideon (born 1300 BC). Not the same as Joash, king of Judah. Scripture gives no dates for him.

people.name: Deborah
people.description: Prophet and judge who held court beneath a palm in the hill country of Ephraim, she summoned Barak and led Israel to victory over Sisera's Canaanite forces. The Song of Deborah in Judges 5 is widely regarded as one of the oldest poems preserved in the Hebrew Bible.
people.dateNotes: Jabin of Hazor oppressed Israel twenty years (Judg 4:3), c. 1305-1285 BC; Deborah and Barak defeated Sisera c. 1285 BC (Ussher), who counts the forty years of rest (Judg 5:31) from Ehud's deliverance. "A mother in Israel" (Judg 5:7) at the victory; birth and death are estimates.

people.name: Barak
people.description: Military commander who fought alongside Deborah against Sisera.
people.dateNotes: Judg 4-5; Heb 11:32. Life dates estimated around the victory over Sisera, c. 1285 BC (Ussher).

people.name: Sisera
people.description: Canaanite general defeated by Deborah and Barak; killed by Jael.
people.dateNotes: Judg 4-5. Killed by Jael on the day of his defeat, c. 1285 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated.

people.name: Heber the Kenite
people.description: Kenite, of the family of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law. He had separated from the other Kenites and pitched his tent near Kedesh, at peace with Jabin of Hazor; his wife Jael killed Sisera.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Husband of Jael (born about 1315 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him, and the Kenite clan is described as living at peace with Jabins Canaanite kingdom at the time of Sisera's defeat (about 1285 BC).

scripture.context: A Kenite who had pitched his tent near Kedesh
Jael is his wife; his house is at peace with Jabin

people.name: Jael
people.description: Kenite woman who killed Sisera by driving a tent peg through his temple.
people.dateNotes: Judg 4:17-22; 5:24-27. Killed Sisera with a tent peg, c. 1285 BC (Ussher). Life dates estimated.

people.name: Gideon
people.description: Judge called from threshing wheat in a winepress to deliver Israel from Midian, he routed a vast host with only three hundred men so the glory would be God's alone. Also named Jerubbaal; a jar inscription bearing that rare name was unearthed at Khirbet al-Rai in the Judean foothills.
people.dateNotes: Midian oppressed Israel seven years (Judg 6:1), c. 1252-1245 BC; Gideon's victory c. 1245 BC (Ussher). Ussher counts the forty years of quiet "in the days of Gideon" (Judg 8:28) from Deborah's victory, so Gideon died c. 1236 BC, when Abimelech seized power. His age is not given: his firstborn Jether was still a youth at the victory (Judg 8:20), and he died "in a good old age" (Judg 8:32). Birth is an estimate. Annals §356-357.

people.name: Tola
people.description: A man of Issachar, son of Puah, who lived at Shamir in Mount Ephraim and judged Israel twenty-three years after Abimelech (Judg 10:1-2).
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel 23 years (Judg 10:1-2), c. 1233-1210 BC (Ussher), and died. Birth estimated. Annals §360, §366.

people.name: Gaal, son of Ebed
people.description: Man who came to Shechem with his brothers and stirred its men against Abimelech. He was defeated by Zebul and Abimelech and driven out of the city.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Active during Abimelech's three-year reign, about 1236-1233 BC (Judg 9:22-41; Ussher), placed as an adult of about forty. His birth and death are not recorded. Nothing is said of his tribe.

scripture.context: Leads Shechem's revolt against Abimelech and is expelled

people.name: Abimelech
people.description: Son of Gideon who made himself king; killed at Thebez.
people.dateNotes: Son of Gideon's concubine in Shechem (Judg 8:31). Made king at Shechem after Gideon's death, c. 1236 BC; reigned three years (Judg 9:22) and was killed at Thebez c. 1233 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated. Annals §358-360.

people.name: Jair
people.description: Judge of Israel for 22 years; had 30 sons who rode 30 donkeys.
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel 22 years (Judg 10:3-5), c. 1210-1188 BC (Ussher). Ussher begins the eighteen-year oppression by the Ammonites and Philistines (Judg 10:7-8) c. 1206 BC, in Jair's time, although the narrative tells it after his burial, and ends it with Jephthah's victory in 1188 BC, the year Jair died. Birth estimated. Annals §366-370.

people.name: Gilead, father of Jephthah
people.description: Father of Jephthah the Gileadite. The text names him as the father, while also noting that Jephthah's mother was a prostitute; his other sons drove Jephthah out.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty years before Jephthah (born 1225 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him. The name is also that of a region east of the Jordan.

people.name: Boaz
people.description: Kinsman-redeemer who married Ruth; ancestor of David.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated: a kinsman of Elimelech, much older than Ruth (Ruth 2:1; 3:10), father of Obed c. 1170 BC. Matthew names Rahab of Jericho (1451 BC) as his mother (Matt 1:5); as that is nearly three centuries before Ruth's story, the link Salmon-Boaz is generally taken to be abbreviated, "begat" meaning "was ancestor of".

people.name: Ibzan
people.description: Judge of Israel from Bethlehem for 7 years; had 30 sons and 30 daughters.
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel seven years after Jephthah (Judg 12:8-10), c. 1182-1175 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated; he had married off thirty sons and thirty daughters.

people.name: Abdon
people.description: Son of Hillel the Pirathonite, of Ephraim, who judged Israel eight years; he had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy ass colts (Judg 12:13-15).
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel eight years (Judg 12:13-15), c. 1165-1157 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated; he had grandsons of riding age. Annals §377-378.

people.name: Elimelech
people.description: Man of Bethlehem who took his wife Naomi and sons Mahlon and Chilion to Moab in a famine and died there. Boaz later redeemed his land.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about ten years before Naomi (born 1225 BC); he died in Moab, within the period of the judges, before his sons (Ruth 1:1-5). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Goes to Moab with Naomi and their sons and dies there
Boaz buys all that was Elimelech's

people.name: Jephthah
people.description: Gileadite warrior, driven out by his half-brothers, who was recalled to lead Gilead against the Ammonites and defeated them. His rash vow cost him his only daughter, and he afterwards fought the men of Ephraim (Judg 11:1-12:7).
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel six years (Judg 12:7), c. 1188-1182 BC (Ussher), after defeating the Ammonites. His "three hundred years" since Israel took Heshbon (Judg 11:26; Heshbon taken 1452 BC) are about 264 on this reckoning, so a round figure; reconstructions that run the Ammonite and Philistine oppressions together (Judg 10:7) date him several decades later. Birth estimated; he had a grown daughter at the victory.

people.name: Naomi
people.description: Ruth's mother-in-law who returned from Moab to Bethlehem.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. Of Bethlehem; returned from Moab a widow, too old to remarry (Ruth 1:12), and nursed her grandson Obed (Ruth 4:16), c. 1170 BC on these estimates. The book is set "when the judges ruled" (Ruth 1:1) without saying which judge.

scripture.context: Husband Elimelech; sons Mahlon and Chilion

people.name: Elon
people.description: A Zebulonite who judged Israel ten years and was buried at Aijalon in Zebulun (Judg 12:11-12).
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel ten years (Judg 12:11-12), c. 1175-1165 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated. Annals §374, §377.

people.name: Eli
people.description: High priest at Shiloh who judged Israel forty years and brought up the boy Samuel. His failure to restrain his sons Hophni and Phinehas brought judgment on his house, and he died at 98 when news came that the ark had been taken (1 Sam 1-4).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1214 BC; judged Israel forty years (1 Sam 4:18), c. 1157-1116 BC, following Abdon, and died aged 98 on hearing that the ark was taken (1 Sam 4:15-18), 1116 BC. Annals §365, §378, §386.

scripture.context: Dies on hearing of his son's death and the ark's capture

people.name: Abiel
people.description: Benjamite, grandfather of King Saul and of Abner. His sons Kish and Ner were brothers, so Saul and Abner were cousins.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before his sons Kish and Ner. 1 Samuel 9:1 and 14:51 call both of them sons of Abiel; 1 Chronicles 8:33 and 9:39 give a different arrangement (Ner begat Kish; 9:36 lists them as brothers), and the genealogies are hard to reconcile. This timeline follows 1 Samuel.

people.name: Manoah
people.description: Father of Samson; visited by the Angel of the LORD.
people.dateNotes: Judg 13-14; 16:31. Life dates estimated: Samson was born c. 1155 BC, Manoah went with him to Timnah (Judg 14:5), and Samson was buried in Manoah's tomb (Judg 16:31).

people.name: Mahlon
people.description: Elder son of Elimelech and Naomi, who married Ruth the Moabite and died childless in Moab. Boaz married Ruth to raise up his name.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about twenty-five years after his parents' birth; he married about ten years before dying in Moab (Ruth 1:4-5). His death is not dated.

scripture.context: Dies in Moab; Ruth is his widow
Ruth is bought to raise up his name

people.name: Chilion
people.description: Younger son of Elimelech and Naomi, husband of Orpah. He died in Moab without children.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born just after Mahlon; he died in Moab about ten years after the marriages (Ruth 1:4-5). His death is not dated.

scripture.context: Dies in Moab; Orpah is his widow

people.name: Orpah
people.description: Moabite woman, wife of Chilion. After his death she kissed Naomi goodbye and stayed in Moab while her sister-in-law Ruth went on to Bethlehem.
people.dateNotes: Estimate; she married about the time Ruth did (Ruth 1:4). Scripture gives no dates for her.

people.name: Ruth
people.description: Moabite great-grandmother of David.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. The story is set "in the days when the judges ruled" (Ruth 1:1); placing Obed's birth c. 1170 BC leaves a natural three generations to David (b. 1085 BC). Boaz praised her for not following young men (Ruth 3:10).

scripture.context: Wife of Mahlon, bought by Boaz

people.name: Elkanah, father of Samuel
people.description: Man of Ramathaim in the hills of Ephraim who went up yearly to Shiloh with his wives Hannah and Peninnah. He was the father of Samuel.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about forty years before Samuel (born 1150 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him. 1 Samuel 1:1 calls him an Ephrathite, while 1 Chronicles 6:27-28 lists a Levite Elkanah as father of Samuel; the sources differ on his tribe.

scripture.context: Husband of Hannah; goes up to Shiloh
Son of Jeroham; father of Shemuel

people.name: Peninnah
people.description: Second wife of Elkanah, with sons and daughters, who provoked Hannah each year because Hannah had no children.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. She was Elkanah's wife with several children before Samuel's birth in 1150 BC (1 Sam 1:2-7), placed a few years after him. Death not recorded.

events.role: Elkanah's other wife, whose taunts led to Hannah's prayer

scripture.context: Elkanah's second wife, who provokes Hannah

people.name: Hannah
people.description: Mother of Samuel; prayed fervently for a child and dedicated him to God.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated (1 Sam 1-2); mother of Samuel (born c. 1150 BC).

people.name: Hophni
people.description: Elder son of Eli, priest at Shiloh with his brother Phinehas. The two abused the sacrifices and were condemned by a prophet; both died on the day the Philistines took the ark.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born while Eli (born 1214 BC) was in his thirties. His death in the battle in which the ark was captured (1116 BC) is dated by that event (1 Sam 4:11).

scripture.context: Priest at Shiloh, son of Eli
Doomed to die with his brother in one day
Slain when the ark is taken

people.name: Phinehas, son of Eli
people.description: Younger son of Eli, priest at Shiloh with Hophni. He died in the battle in which the ark was taken, and his wife died giving birth to Ichabod on hearing the news.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born shortly after Hophni. His death in the battle in which the ark was captured (1116 BC) is dated by that event (1 Sam 4:11). Not the same as Phinehas, son of Eleazar.

scripture.context: Priest at Shiloh, son of Eli
Dies when the ark is taken; Ichabod is born

people.name: Obed
people.description: Son of Boaz and Ruth; father of Jesse, grandfather of David. Central link in the Messianic lineage.
people.dateNotes: Ruth 4:13-17, 21-22; 1 Chr 2:12; Matt 1:5. Life dates estimated.

people.name: Kish
people.description: Benjamite, "a mighty man of power," father of King Saul. Saul was sent out to look for his father's lost donkeys on the day Samuel met him.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Saul (born 1135 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Son of Abiel; father of Saul
Among the sons of the father of Gibeon

people.name: Ner
people.description: Benjamite, brother of Kish and uncle of King Saul. His son Abner commanded Saul's army.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born near his brother Kish, about forty years before Abner (born 1130 BC). The KJV of 1 Samuel 14:50 calls Abner "Saul's uncle," but verse 51 shows Ner to be the uncle and Abner the cousin. 1 Chronicles 8:33 places Ner as Kish's father; this timeline follows 1 Samuel.

scripture.context: Father of Abner; son of Abiel
Ner, in the line of Saul
Ner, in the line of Saul

people.name: Samson
people.description: Nazirite judge endowed with extraordinary strength, he battled the Philistines single-handedly until Delilah's betrayal cost him his hair, his eyes, and his freedom. In death he toppled Dagon's temple, and his story mirrors Israel's own struggle with compromised devotion.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born c. 1155 BC, soon after the Philistines' forty years of domination began (Judg 13:1); judged Israel twenty years "in the days of the Philistines" (Judg 15:20; 16:31), c. 1137-1117 BC, and died at Gaza in 1117 BC, the year before Eli. Annals §380, §382, §384.

people.name: Samuel
people.description: Last of the judges and first of the great prophets, dedicated at the Shiloh sanctuary in answer to Hannah's prayer. He anointed both Saul and David, guiding Israel's passage from tribal confederation to monarchy while insisting that obedience outweighs sacrifice.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated (Ussher gives no year). Serving Eli at Shiloh as a child (1 Sam 1-3), he judged Israel after Eli's death in 1116 BC, routed the Philistines at Mizpah c. 1096 BC (1 Sam 7), anointed Saul in 1095 BC and David c. 1063 BC, and died c. 1060 BC, before David's second flight to Gath (1 Sam 25:1; 27:1-2).

scripture.context: Dedicated spoils to the sanctuary treasury

people.name: Delilah
people.description: A woman of the valley of Sorek whom Samson loved. Bribed by the Philistine lords, she drew out the secret of his strength and betrayed him (Judg 16:4-21); Scripture does not say whether she was a Philistine or an Israelite.
people.dateNotes: Judg 16:4-21. Betrayed Samson c. 1117 BC (Ussher). Life dates are estimates.

people.name: Jesse
people.description: A Bethlehemite of the tribe of Judah, grandson of Ruth and Boaz, and father of eight sons, the youngest of whom Samuel anointed as king. Isaiah's promise of a shoot from the stump of Jesse made his name shorthand for the messianic hope Christians see fulfilled in Jesus.
people.dateNotes: 1 Sam 16:1-13; 17:12-14; Ruth 4:22; Isa 11:1, 10; Matt 1:5-6. Life dates estimated: "an old man in the days of Saul" (1 Sam 17:12), father of David (b. 1085 BC) in his old age.

people.name: Saul
people.description: Israel's first king, a tall Benjaminite anointed by Samuel, who won early victories over Ammon and the Philistines. His impatience and disobedience cost his house the throne, and his tragic decline beside David's rise ended on Mount Gilboa, where he fell in battle.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned forty years (Acts 13:21), 1095-1055 BC, and fell at Gilboa. His age at accession is not given (the Hebrew of 1 Sam 13:1 is defective); the birth year is an estimate allowing for a son, Jonathan, who commanded a thousand men in Saul's second year (1 Sam 13:2). Mainstream scholarship dates his reign c. 1050-1010 BC.

scripture.context: Kish was the father of Saul
Dedicated spoils to the sanctuary treasury

people.name: Ahitub, father of Zadok
people.description: Priest, father of Zadok, who served David and anointed Solomon. He is not the Ahitub who was the grandson of Eli.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about forty-five years before Zadok (born 1090 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him. 1 Chronicles 6:8 places Zadok in the line of Eleazar, whereas Eli's Ahitub was of the line of Ithamar.

people.name: Nahash king of Ammon
people.description: King of the Ammonites who besieged Jabesh-gilead and offered terms of putting out every right eye, until Saul rescued the city. Later he showed David kindness, so that David tried to comfort his son Hanun when Nahash died.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. He was reigning when Saul was made king (1095 BC on this timeline, 1 Sam 11) and died some years before David's embassy, which Ussher dates to 1038 BC (2 Sam 10:1-2). That spans nearly sixty years, so either his reign was very long or the two events are only loosely tied to the dates given.

events.role: King of Ammon who besieged Jabesh-gilead

scripture.context: Remembered for his kindness to David

people.name: Abner
people.description: Commander of Saul's army; supported Ish-bosheth then defected to David. Killed by Joab.
people.dateNotes: Birth estimated: son of Ner, Saul's uncle (1 Sam 14:50-51), and already captain of Saul's army early in the reign. Killed by Joab at Hebron in 1048 BC (Ussher; 2 Sam 3:27). Annals §415.

scripture.context: Dedicated spoils to the sanctuary treasury

people.name: Ahinoam, wife of Saul
people.description: Wife of King Saul, daughter of Ahimaaz. The text names her as his wife but does not say which of his children were hers. She is a different woman from David's wife Ahinoam of Jezreel.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Roughly the age of Saul (born 1135 BC), who had grown sons by the time he became king. Scripture gives no dates for her.

people.name: Joel, son of Samuel
people.description: Eldest son of Samuel. With his brother Abiah he judged at Beer-sheba, but they took bribes and perverted justice, and the elders used their conduct to ask for a king.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born while Samuel (born 1150 BC) was in his twenties; Samuel made his sons judges when he was old (1 Sam 8:1-2), shortly before Saul's anointing in 1095 BC. 1 Chronicles 6:28 gives the firstborn's name as Vashni; the two names are commonly reconciled but the text does not say so.

people.name: Abiah, son of Samuel
people.description: Second son of Samuel, judge at Beer-sheba with his brother Joel. Their corruption led Israel's elders to ask Samuel for a king.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born shortly after Joel; Samuel made his sons judges when he was old (1 Sam 8:1-2). His death is not recorded.

scripture.context: Listed among the sons of Samuel
Samuel's second son; judge at Beer-sheba

people.name: Eliab, son of Jesse
people.description: Eldest son of Jesse. Samuel took him for the Lord's anointed because of his height, but God had chosen another; later he rebuked David for coming to the battle line against Goliath.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before David (born 1085 BC), as the eldest of Jesse's eight sons. Scripture gives no dates for him.

events.role: rebukes David at the battle line

scripture.context: Passed over when Samuel looks for the king
Eldest of the three sons with Saul's army

people.name: Abinadab, son of Jesse
people.description: Second son of Jesse. He was passed over by Samuel and followed Saul to the battle against the Philistines.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born between Eliab and Shammah (about 1120 to 1114 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Passed over when Samuel looks for the king
Second of the three sons with Saul's army

people.name: Ichabod
people.description: Son of Phinehas and grandson of Eli, born as his mother died after hearing that the ark was lost. She named him Ichabod, "the glory has departed." His brother Ahitub appears in 1 Samuel 14:3.
people.dateNotes: Born at the time the ark was captured (1116 BC; 1 Sam 4:19-21). The text does not record his death. Ussher, Annals §386.

events.role: born on the day the ark was taken

scripture.context: Born as the ark is taken; named Ichabod

people.name: Jonathan
people.description: Saul's son and David's closest friend; died at Gilboa.
people.dateNotes: Birth estimated: he commanded a thousand men in Saul's second year (1 Sam 13:2-3), c. 1093 BC, and had a five-year-old son when he died (2 Sam 4:4). Died with Saul at Gilboa, 1055 BC (Ussher; 1 Sam 31:2).

people.name: Ahimelech the priest of Nob
people.description: Priest at Nob, son of Ahitub, who gave the fleeing David the holy bread and the sword of Goliath. Saul had him and the priests of Nob killed, which Doeg the Edomite carried out. His son Abiathar escaped. Of the house of Eli, in the priestly line of Ithamar.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. He was an established priest when David came to Nob, around 1060 BC (the tour dates that visit), and Saul killed him soon after (1 Sam 22:18). Birth is a guess around that. Ahitub and Ahimelech belong to Eli's house through Phinehas (1 Sam 14:3; 22:9); 1 Chr 24:3 places an Ahimelech among the sons of Ithamar, though that may be Abiathar's son.

scripture.context: Gives David the holy bread and Goliath's sword
Accused by Doeg and killed by Saul
An Ahimelech counted among the sons of Ithamar

people.name: Shammah, son of Jesse
people.description: Third son of Jesse, passed over by Samuel and a soldier in Saul's army. The Chronicles list him as Shimma; his son Jonadab, a wily man, advised Amnon.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty years before David (born 1085 BC). The identification of Shammah (1 Sam 16:9; 17:13) with Shimma (1 Chron 2:13) and Shimeah (2 Sam 13:3) is the usual reading; the text gives the names separately.

scripture.context: Passed over when Samuel looks for the king
Third of the three sons with Saul's army

people.name: Ahithophel
people.description: David's counselor who defected to Absalom; hanged himself when his advice was rejected.
people.dateNotes: 2 Sam 15:12, 31; 16:20-17:23. Hanged himself during Absalom's revolt, 1023 BC. If Bathsheba's father Eliam (2 Sam 11:3) is the Eliam son of Ahithophel among David's mighty men (2 Sam 23:34), he was her grandfather; the birth year is an estimate allowing for that. Ussher, Annals §442-444.

people.name: Merab
people.description: Saul's elder daughter, offered to David as a reward for fighting the Philistines but given instead to Adriel the Meholathite.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born before her younger sister Michal (born 1085 BC) and after Jonathan (born 1115 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her.

scripture.context: Promised to David, given to Adriel

people.name: Jether, father of Amasa
people.description: Husband of Abigail, David's sister, and father of Amasa. 1 Chronicles calls him an Ishmaelite; 2 Samuel calls him Ithra an Israelite.
people.dateNotes: Estimate; born slightly before his wife Abigail (born about 1106 BC). The two names and descriptions (Jether the Ishmaelite, 1 Chron 2:17; Ithra the Israelite, 2 Sam 17:25) are usually taken to be one man, with a difference in the manuscripts.

people.name: Jonathan, uncle of David
people.description: David's uncle, described as a counselor, a wise man and a scribe.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Called David's uncle, so born before David (about 1085 BC); his own father is not named.

people.name: Zeruiah
people.description: Sister of David and mother of the three brothers Joab, Abishai and Asahel, who served in his army. The text calls her David's sister but does not name her husband or say which parent she shared with David.
people.dateNotes: Estimate, born before her son Joab (born 1085 BC). 1 Chronicles 2:16 calls Zeruiah and Abigail "sisters" of Jesse's sons. 2 Samuel 17:25 calls Abigail the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah, so Zeruiah and Abigail may have had a different father or mother from David; no parent is recorded for her here.

scripture.context: Sister of Jesse's sons; mother of Abishai, Joab and Asahel

people.name: Nethaneel, son of Jesse
people.description: Fourth son of Jesse and brother of David (1 Chr 2:14-15).
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Fourth of Jesse's seven sons in Chronicles, between Shammah (born 1114 BC) and David (1085 BC); no dates recorded.

people.name: Abigail, sister of David
people.description: Sister of David and of Zeruiah, mother of Amasa, whom Absalom made commander of his army. She is a different woman from Abigail the wife of Nabal and David.
people.dateNotes: Estimate, born before her son Amasa. 1 Chronicles 2:16 calls her a sister of Jesse's sons; 2 Samuel 17:25 calls her the daughter of Nahash. The text does not reconcile the two, and no parent is recorded for her here.

scripture.context: Sister of Jesse's sons; mother of Amasa
Daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah

people.name: Barzillai the Gileadite
people.description: Aged and wealthy man of Rogelim in Gilead who fed David and his people at Mahanaim during Absalom's revolt. He escorted the king over the Jordan but declined to live at court, asking that his servant Chimham go in his place.
people.dateNotes: He was eighty years old when David returned after Absalom's revolt (2 Sam 19:32, 35), 1023 BC on this timeline, so born 1103 BC. His death is not recorded.

people.name: Raddai, son of Jesse
people.description: Fifth son of Jesse and brother of David (1 Chr 2:14-15).
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Fifth of Jesse's seven sons in Chronicles, between Shammah (born 1114 BC) and David (1085 BC); no dates recorded.

people.name: Nabal
people.description: Wealthy but foolish man married to Abigail; refused to help David. Died after the LORD struck him.
people.dateNotes: 1 Sam 25:2-42. Died about ten days after his feast (1 Sam 25:38), soon after Samuel's death and before David fled to Gath, c. 1060 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Elihu, brother of David
people.description: Brother of David and ruler of Judah in 1 Chronicles 27:18; some identify him with Eliab, David's eldest brother.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born after Jesse's sons Eliab, Abinadab and Shammah, before David (about 1085 BC). The text does not say whether he is the same man as Eliab.

scripture.context: Ruler of Judah, one of the brethren of David

people.name: Ish-bosheth
people.description: Saul's surviving son; made king over Israel by Abner while David reigned in Judah.
people.dateNotes: Scripture: forty when he began to reign, and reigned two years (2 Sam 2:10). Ussher, Annals 409: he was made king at Mahanaim in 1055 BC, the year of Saul's death, so born 1095 BC, the year Saul became king; the two years are the two years of peace with David, followed by a long war (2 Sam 3:1; Annals 411), and he was murdered in 1048 BC (Annals 416), just before the tribes made David king (2 Sam 4-5). Others place his two years at the end of David's seven and a half years at Hebron, making him born c. 1090 BC.

people.name: Eliam, father of Bathsheba
people.description: Father of Bathsheba, wife of Uriah and later of David. 2 Samuel 23:34 names an Eliam son of Ahithophel among David's mighty men; the text does not say that the two are the same man.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty years before Bathsheba (born 1065 BC). 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives her father as Ammiel, a reversal of the same name. Scripture gives no dates for him.

people.name: Ozem, son of Jesse
people.description: Sixth son of Jesse and brother of David (1 Chr 2:14-15).
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Sixth of Jesse's seven sons in Chronicles, between Shammah (born 1114 BC) and David (1085 BC); no dates recorded.

people.name: Abigail
people.description: Wise woman who became David's wife after the death of Nabal.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. Married David after Nabal's death, c. 1060 BC (1 Sam 25); with him at Ziklag and Hebron (1 Sam 30:5; 2 Sam 2:2) and mother of his second son (2 Sam 3:3). Death unrecorded.

people.name: Rizpah, concubine of Saul
people.description: Daughter of Aiah and concubine of Saul. Abner's taking of her sparked his break with Ish-bosheth. Years later she kept watch over the bodies of her two sons and five of Saul's grandsons through a whole season, driving off birds and beasts, until David had the bones buried.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. She was Saul's concubine before 1055 BC and her sons were grown men when the Gibeonites executed them, about 1018 BC (2 Sam 21:8-10, Ussher). Death not recorded. Her son Mephibosheth is a different person from Jonathan's son of the same name.

scripture.context: Guards the bodies of the executed sons

people.name: Rehabiah, son of Eliezer
people.description: Only son of Eliezer son of Moses; his sons were very many.
people.dateNotes: Compressed genealogy: placed before his descendants of David's day.

people.name: David
people.description: Shepherd of Bethlehem who felled Goliath and rose to the throne after Saul, uniting the tribes and taking Jerusalem as his capital. Psalmist and covenant king promised an everlasting dynasty, his house is named on the Tel Dan stele, the earliest extrabiblical witness to his royal line.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1085 BC; anointed by Samuel at Bethlehem c. 1063 BC; king at Hebron aged 30 in 1055 BC and over all Israel from 1048 BC; reigned forty years, seven and a half at Hebron and thirty-three at Jerusalem (2 Sam 5:4-5), and died 1015 BC. Mainstream scholarship dates his reign c. 1010-970 BC.

people.name: Nathan the prophet
people.description: Prophet during David and Solomon's reigns.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. Active from the Davidic covenant (c. 1044 BC, 2 Sam 7) to Solomon's anointing (1015 BC, 1 Kgs 1).

events.role: prophet who helped secure the succession

people.name: Joab
people.description: Commander of David's army; politically shrewd and ruthless.
people.dateNotes: Birth estimated; son of David's sister Zeruiah (1 Chr 2:16). Executed by Benaiah at Solomon's command early in his reign, 1014 BC (Ussher; 1 Kgs 2:28-34).

people.name: Michal
people.description: Saul's daughter; David's first wife who helped him escape.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. Saul's younger daughter (1 Sam 14:49), married to David after his victory over Goliath (c. 1063-1062 BC), given to Phaltiel, and returned to David in 1048 BC (2 Sam 3:14-16). Childless (2 Sam 6:23). Death unrecorded.

scripture.context: Watched David dance as the ark came in

people.name: Ahinoam of Jezreel
people.description: One of David's wives, taken during his years as a fugitive from Saul. She bore his first son, Amnon.
people.dateNotes: Estimate, a contemporary of David (born 1085 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her.

scripture.context: Taken by David as a wife

people.name: Abiathar
people.description: Son of Ahimelech and the one priest of Nob to escape Saul's massacre. He fled to David, served as his priest and, with Zadok, held the priesthood. He backed Adonijah and Solomon removed him to Anathoth, ending the line of Eli's house in the priesthood as God had said at Shiloh.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Already grown when he escaped from Nob (about 1060 BC) and still serving when he joined Adonijah in 1015 BC (1 Kgs 1:7), when Ussher dates his removal to 1014 BC. His death is not recorded. Ussher counts him of Ithamar's line, so the priesthood passed back to Eleazar's line in Zadok.

people.name: Asaph
people.description: Levite of the Gershonite family, son of Berechiah, whom David appointed chief of the singers before the ark. His sons formed one of the three guilds of Temple musicians, and Psalm 50 and Psalms 73-83 carry his name.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Already a leading Levite in 1045 BC, when David set the singers in order (1 Chr 15:17-19), so born about 1085 BC. His death is not recorded; the sons of Asaph are still singing in Solomon's day (2 Chr 5:12) and later reigns.

people.name: Heman the singer
people.description: Kohathite Levite, called the king's seer, who led one of the three guilds of Temple singers and had fourteen sons and three daughters. He is named as a son of Joel and, in a traditional reading, grandson of the prophet Samuel. Psalm 88 is attributed to Heman the Ezrahite, whom some identify with him.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. A leading singer in 1045 BC (1 Chr 15:17), so born about 1085 BC. Chronicles calls his father Joel, son of Shemuel (1 Chr 6:33), usually read as Samuel (born 1150 BC), but his father is not in the table. Death not recorded.

people.name: Abishai
people.description: Son of Zeruiah, nephew of David, and one of his best-known commanders. He went with David into Saul's camp by night and later saved David's life in battle.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born between his brothers Joab (born 1085 BC) and Asahel. His death is not recorded in Scripture.

people.name: Asahel
people.description: Youngest son of Zeruiah and a nephew of David, "light of foot as a wild roe." He pursued Abner after the battle at Gibeon and was killed by him, which later led Joab to kill Abner.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born after Joab (1085 BC) and Abishai. He was killed in the first years of David's reign at Hebron, about 1055 BC (2 Sam 2:18-23).

scripture.context: Third of the three sons of Zeruiah

people.name: Obed-edom the Gittite
people.description: Man of Gath in whose house the ark rested three months after Uzzah's death. God blessed his household, which encouraged David to bring the ark on to Jerusalem. Chronicles later lists an Obed-edom among the Levite gatekeepers and singers, and many readers take them to be the same man; others distinguish him from Obed-edom son of Jeduthun.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. A grown man with a household in 1045 BC; still serving as a gatekeeper when the ark was settled (1 Chr 15:24; 16:38). Called a Gittite from Gath or Gath-rimmon, a Levite city, which is why Chronicles can list him as a Levite. Death not recorded.

people.name: Jeduthun

people.dateNotes: Estimate. Serving as a musician when David arranged the Levites (1 Chr 15-16, about 1045 BC), so born about 1080 BC. The Ethan identification is the common reading, not stated outright. Death not recorded.

people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born after his mother Abigail (born about 1106 BC); an adult commander by Absalom's revolt (1023 BC). His death is not dated in this table.

people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.dateNotes: 2 Sam 15:24-29; 1 Kgs 1:32-45; Ezek 44:15. Life dates estimated; "a young man mighty of valour" when he came with the tribes to David at Hebron (1 Chr 12:27-28), 1048 BC (Ussher, Annals 413), so born about 1075 BC. Anointed Solomon with Nathan in 1015 BC (1 Kgs 1:39; Annals 457).

people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born before Absalom (born 1053 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her. Not the same as Maacah, daughter of Absalom, Rehoboam's wife.

people.name: Hanun king of Ammon

people.dateNotes: Estimate. Reigned from about 1038 BC, when his father died (Ussher; 2 Sam 10:1-4). Birth is a guess around that; his death is not recorded.

people.name: Hiram
people.description: King of Tyre; ally of David and Solomon. Supplied materials for the Temple.
people.dateNotes: On Ussher's dates Hiram sent builders to David c. 1046 BC (2 Sam 5:11) and still dealt with Solomon c. 992 BC (1 Kgs 9:10-14). Josephus (Against Apion 1.18, from Menander of Ephesus) gives him a reign of 34 years and a life of 53, which mainstream chronology places c. 980-947 BC; on that reckoning 2 Sam 5:11 is told out of sequence. Life dates are estimates.

people.name: Shimei

people.name: Hushai
people.description: David's friend who pretended to join Absalom and thwarted Ahithophel's counsel.
people.dateNotes: 2 Sam 15:32-37; 16:16-17:16. Active in Absalom's revolt, 1023 BC (Ussher, Annals 442-445). Life dates estimated; Scripture gives no ages.

people.name: Haggith
people.description: Wife of David and mother of Adonijah, who tried to take the throne before Solomon was crowned.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born before Adonijah (born 1051 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her.

people.name: Benaiah, son of Jehoiada
people.description: Warrior from Kabzeel whom David set over his guard, the Cherethites and Pelethites. He took part in anointing Solomon, executed Joab and Shimei's sentence at Solomon's command, and succeeded Joab as head of the army. Not the later priest Jehoiada of Athaliah's day.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. He was a famous mighty man by the later years of David and was captain of the guard in 1015 BC (1 Kgs 1:32-38). Ussher places Joab's death and Benaiah's promotion in 1014 BC. His death is not recorded.

Scripture's sequence: Amnon's crime, two full years to the sheepshearing (2 Sam 13:23), three years in Geshur (13:38), two full years in Jerusalem before seeing the king (14:28), then revolt "after forty years" (15:7; the Septuagint, Syriac and Josephus read four). people.name: Solomon
people.description: Son of David famed for God-given wisdom, he built the first temple in Jerusalem and presided over a golden age of trade, building, and proverbs. Monumental gates at Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer have long been associated with his projects, yet his foreign marriages sowed the kingdom's division.
people.dateNotes: Scripture: reigned forty years (1 Kgs 11:42); began the Temple in his 4th year, the 480th year from the Exodus (1 Kgs 6:1), and finished it in seven years (6:38), then built his own house thirteen years (7:1). Ussher, Annals 435, 459, 465: born 1034 BC to Bathsheba after the death of her first child by David (2 Sam 12:24), so about 19 at his accession; reign 1015-975 BC; Temple begun 1012 BC and finished 1005 BC; palace 1005-992 BC. Rehoboam was 41 when Solomon died (1 Kgs 14:21), so born the year before Solomon took the throne (Annals 455). Mainstream scholarship dates his reign c. 970-931 BC.

people.name: Nathan son of David
people.description: Son of David and Bathsheba. Ancestor of Jesus in Luke 3:31. Not the prophet Nathan.
people.dateNotes: 2 Sam 5:14; 1 Chr 3:5; Luke 3:31. Born in Jerusalem to Bathsheba. 1 Chr 3:5 lists him before Solomon, but Solomon was evidently her first son after the death of the child of 2 Sam 12 (c. 1034 BC), so a birth c. 1030 BC is estimated. Not to be confused with Nathan the prophet (2 Sam 7).

people.name: Asa
people.description: Good king of Judah who removed idols and sought the Lord.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 955-914 BC (41 years, 1 Kgs 15:9-10), from the 20th year of Jeroboam. Birth estimated: his son Jehoshaphat was 35 when Asa died (1 Kgs 22:42) and Asa was diseased in his feet in his old age (1 Kgs 15:23). Thiele: 911-870 BC. 1 Kings 15:9-24; 2 Chronicles 14-16. Scripture gives Asa's accession in the 20th year of Jeroboam (1 Kgs 15:9), while Jeroboam's 22 years (14:20) and Nadab's accession in Asa's 2nd year (15:25) make Asa's first year Jeroboam's 21st; Ussher's harmonising choice (Abijah's 3 years run 958-955) puts Asa's first year at 955 BC, in Jeroboam's 20th year as it ended. The 36th year of 2 Chr 16:1 is counted from the division of the kingdom, i.e. Asa's 16th (940 BC, Annals Sec. 496), since Baasha died in Asa's 26th year (1 Kgs 16:6-8).

Birth estimated. Scripture: Omri began in Asa's 31st year and reigned 12 years (1 Kgs 16:23), yet Ahab began in Asa's 38th (16:29), only seven years later. Ussher's choice (Annals Sec. 500-503): the 12 years are counted from 929 BC, Asa's 27th year, when the army made him king; Tibni's rival party held half the people for about four years until Omri prevailed in the 31st.

people.name: Amon, governor of the city under Ahab
people.description: Governor to whom Ahab ordered Micaiah to be taken after his prophecy of defeat.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Elijah
people.description: Prophet of Gilead who confronted Ahab and the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, where fire from heaven vindicated the Lord. Fed by ravens and met by a still small voice at Horeb, he was taken up in a whirlwind, and Malachi promises his return before the great day of the Lord.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: active during Ahab's reign (918-897 BC). Translated c. 896 BC (2 Kgs 2:11), early in Joram of Israel's reign. 2 Chr 21:12-15 records a writing from Elijah to Jehoram of Judah (reigned from 892 BC): either it was written before his translation or the dating is uncertain. Born c. 930 BC (estimated).

events.role: Prophet sustained by God in the drought
Prophet who met God at Horeb
Pronounced judgment on Ahab and Jezebel

people.name: Naaman
people.description: Syrian army commander healed of leprosy by Elisha.
people.dateNotes: Healed during the reign of Jehoram of Israel, c. 890 BC on Ussher's chain (2 Kgs 5-6). Birth estimated; death unrecorded, estimate only.

people.name: Jehonadab son of Rechab
people.description: Zealous ally of Jehu who rode with him in his chariot and helped him destroy the worshippers of Baal in Samaria. He is also the ancestor-figure of the Rechabites, who kept his command never to drink wine, build houses or plant vineyards; Jeremiah later held them up as a model of obedience.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. He met Jehu in 884 BC (2 Kgs 10:15), so was an adult then. Scripture does not give his birth or death. The Rechabites in 1 Chronicles 2:55 are linked to the Kenites.

events.role: Rode with Jehu and helped destroy Baal's worshippers

people.name: Dodavah of Mareshah
people.description: Father of the prophet Eliezer, from Mareshah.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Athaliah
people.description: Wicked queen of Judah who usurped the throne and killed royal heirs.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 884-878 BC (six years, 2 Kgs 11:3), after Ahaziah's death in 884; killed in the seventh year when Joash was crowned (2 Kgs 11:4-16; Annals §535-536). Birth 927 BC from Annals §502 (as it seems, 42 years before her son Ahaziah began to reign in 885). Thiele: 841-835 BC. Called daughter of Ahab (2 Kgs 8:18) and of Omri (8:26), i.e. Ahab's daughter and Omri's granddaughter.

people.name: Segub, youngest son of Hiel
people.description: Youngest son of Hiel, who died when the gates of Jericho were set up.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Jehoram of Judah
people.description: Wicked king of Judah who married Ahab's daughter and led Judah astray.
people.dateNotes: Ussher chain: reigned 892-885 BC (8 years, 2 Kgs 8:16-17), from the fifth year of Joram of Israel while Jehoshaphat was still living; 2 Kgs 1:17 implies an earlier association with his father. Age 32 at accession: born 924 BC; died at about 40 (2 Chr 21:20). Thiele: 848-841 BC, coregent from 853.

people.name: Ahaziah of Israel
people.description: Son of Ahab; wicked king who sought Baal-zebub instead of God.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: began in Jehoshaphat's 17th year as viceroy to his father Ahab (898 BC, 1 Kgs 22:51; Annals Sec. 516), sole king after Ahab's death in 897 and dead in 896 BC; his two years (22:51) were partly with his father, partly alone (Annals Sec. 521). Thiele: 853-852 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Elisha
people.description: Farmer called from the plow to succeed Elijah, receiving a double portion of his spirit. Serving Israel through the reigns of four kings, he healed Naaman's leprosy, multiplied bread and oil, and raised the dead, extending God's mercy to Israelite and foreigner alike.
people.dateNotes: Called by Elijah in Ahab's reign (1 Kgs 19:19-21), before Ahab died in 897 BC; succeeded Elijah c. 896 BC (2 Kgs 2). Died early in the reign of Jehoash of Israel (2 Kgs 13:14-20), c. 839 BC (Ussher). Born c. 920 BC (estimated).

events.role: Prophet who promised water and victory
Sent the prophet who anointed Jehu

people.name: Jehoram of Israel
people.description: Son of Ahab; last king of the Omride dynasty; killed by Jehu.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 896-884 BC (12 years, 2 Kgs 3:1), from Jehoshaphat's 18th year; killed by Jehu (2 Kgs 9:24). Brother of Ahaziah, who had no son (2 Kgs 1:17); the text does not say which was older. Synchronisms: 18th year of Jehoshaphat (2 Kgs 3:1) and 2nd year of Jehoram of Judah (1:17), the latter reconciled by Ussher through Jehoram's earlier viceroyalty (Annals Sec. 515). Thiele: 852-841 BC. Birth estimated.

events.role: King of Israel who led the campaign

people.name: Jehu
people.description: Anointed by Elisha's servant; destroyed the house of Ahab and Baal worship.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 884-856 BC (28 years, 2 Kgs 10:36). Thiele: 841-814 BC; Shalmaneser III's Black Obelisk shows him paying tribute in 841 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Hazael
people.description: King of Aram (Syria) whose accession Elisha foretold in Damascus; he smothered Ben-hadad and reigned in his place, and oppressed Israel through the reigns of Jehu and Jehoahaz.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: king of Aram by 884 BC, when he had recently succeeded Ben-hadad as Elisha foretold (2 Kgs 8:7-15, 28-29; Annals Sec. 533); the accession year (c. 885) is an estimate. He oppressed Israel through the reign of Jehoahaz (856-840 BC; 2 Kgs 10:32; 13:3, 22) and sent a force against Jerusalem in Joash of Judah's last year, 839 BC (2 Kgs 12:17-18; Sec. 544). He was dead when Jehoash of Israel recovered cities from his son Ben-hadad (2 Kgs 13:24-25; Sec. 546), so death is placed c. 838 BC (estimate; was 840). Inscriptions of Shalmaneser III name him king of Damascus by 841 BC; modern dates c. 842-800 BC. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Bidkar, captain of Jehu
people.description: Jehu's officer who rode with him behind Ahab and threw Joram's body into Naboth's field.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Shunammite Woman
people.description: Wealthy woman who provided for Elisha; her son was raised from death by Elisha.
people.dateNotes: 2 Kgs 4:8-37; 8:1-6. Son raised by Elisha early in his ministry (from c. 896 BC per Ussher). Returned from Philistia after a seven-year absence and appealed to the king, probably Jehoram (896-884 BC). Birth and death estimated (death c. 840 BC).

people.name: Mattan, priest of Baal
people.description: Priest of Baal in Jerusalem, killed before his altars after Athaliah fell.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Gehazi
people.description: Servant of Elisha who was struck with leprosy for greed after Naaman's healing.
people.dateNotes: 2 Kgs 4:12-37; 5:20-27; 8:4-5. Struck with leprosy for greed during Elisha's ministry (c. 896-839 BC per Ussher, Annals §523, §545). Still alive when telling the king of Israel, probably Jehoram (896-884 BC), about Elisha (2 Kgs 8:4-5). Birth and death estimated (death c. 840 BC).

people.name: Shimeath the Ammonitess
people.description: Ammonite woman, mother of Jozachar, one of the servants who killed King Joash.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Shimrith the Moabitess
people.description: Moabite woman, mother of Jehozabad; 2 Kings calls her Shomer.
people.dateNotes: Kings reads Shomer for the same name; possibly a spelling variant. Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Ahaziah of Judah
people.description: Son of Jehoram and Athaliah; king of Judah for one year. Killed by Jehu.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 885-884 BC (1 year, 2 Kgs 8:25-26), from the 12th year of Joram of Israel. Age 22 at accession: born 907 BC; 2 Chr 22:2 reads 42, which would make him older than his father and is usually taken as a copyist's error. Killed by Jehu (2 Kgs 9:27-28). Thiele: 841 BC.

events.role: Son whose death began her rule

people.name: Jehoahaz of Israel
people.description: King of Israel, son of Jehu, who reigned seventeen years. Hazael of Aram and his son Ben-hadad oppressed Israel throughout his reign until he besought the Lord, who gave Israel a deliverer (2 Kgs 13:1-9).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 856-840 BC (17 years counted inclusively, 2 Kgs 13:1), from the 23rd year of Joash of Judah. Thiele: 814-798 BC. Birth estimated. Not Jehoahaz (Shallum) of Judah.

people.name: Zechariah, son of Jehoiada
people.description: Priest on whom the Spirit of God came; King Joash had him stoned in the temple court.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Joash of Judah
people.description: Boy king hidden in the Temple; restored proper worship under Jehoiada's guidance.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 878-839 BC (40 years counted inclusively, 2 Kgs 12:1), from the 7th year of Jehu; slain by his servants (2 Kgs 12:20-21). Age 7 at accession (2 Kgs 11:21): born 885 BC. Thiele: 835-796 BC.

events.role: Infant heir hidden in the temple

people.name: Jehoash of Israel
people.description: King of Israel, son of Jehoahaz. He wept over the dying Elisha, struck the ground only three times with the arrows, and so defeated Ben-hadad three times (2 Kgs 13:14-25). He also defeated Amaziah of Judah at Beth-shemesh and broke down part of Jerusalem's wall (2 Kgs 14:8-14).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 16 years (2 Kgs 13:10), 840-825 BC counted from his father Jehoahaz's death; made viceroy in the latter end of the 37th year of Joash of Judah (842 BC, 2 Kgs 13:10; Annals Sec. 542), which accounts for the 37th-year synchronism although Jehoahaz's 17 years from Joash's 23rd end in 840. Amaziah began in Jehoash's 2nd year (14:1) = 839 BC, and Amaziah outlived him by 15 years (14:17). Thiele: 798-782 BC. Birth estimated. Not Joash (Jehoash) of Judah.

people.name: Jozachar, assassin of Joash
people.description: Servant who conspired against King Joash and killed him; called Zabad in Chronicles.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Jehozabad, assassin of Joash
people.description: Servant who conspired with Jozachar to kill King Joash.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Joel
people.description: Prophet who described a locust plague and the Day of the Lord.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §553: prophesied in Judah under Uzziah (810-758 BC) and Jeroboam II, around the 13th Jubilee (808 BC), before Amos. The book names no king and modern dates range from the 9th to the 4th century BC. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Amaziah
people.description: King of Judah who followed the Lord at first but later turned to idols.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 839-810 BC (29 years, 2 Kgs 14:2), from the second year of Jehoash of Israel; he outlived Jehoash by 15 years (14:17) and Jeroboam II began in his 15th year (14:23). Age 25 at accession: born 864 BC. Thiele: 796-767 BC.

people.name: Jeroboam II
people.description: Powerful king of Israel who expanded borders but tolerated idolatry.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: sole reign 825-784 BC (41 years, 2 Kgs 14:23), from Amaziah's 15th year. Ussher also makes him viceroy to his father Jehoash from 836 BC (Annals Sec. 546), counting from which Uzziah's accession in 810 BC falls in Jeroboam's 27th year (2 Kgs 15:1; Sec. 552). Jonah, Amos and Hosea were active in his reign (2 Kgs 14:25; Amos 1:1; Hos 1:1). Thiele: 793-753 BC (coregent from 793). Birth estimated.

events.role: King of Israel who recovered the territory
First king named in his call

people.name: Jonah
people.description: Prophet sent to Nineveh; swallowed by a great fish after fleeing.
people.dateNotes: Foretold the restoration of Israel's borders achieved by Jeroboam II (2 Kgs 14:25), who reigned 825-784 BC on Ussher's chain; the mission to Nineveh is undated. Birth and death estimated (death c. 750 BC).

people.name: Uzziah
people.description: Good king of Judah who became proud and was struck with leprosy.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §547: born 826 BC, 16 at accession (2 Kgs 15:2). §552: reigned 810-759 BC (52 years), succeeding Amaziah in the 27th year of Jeroboam II reckoned from a coregency. §584: died in 759 BC, the year of Isaiah's vision (Isa 6:1); Jotham succeeded him. §564: struck with leprosy when an old man, soon after Menahem took the throne of Israel (about 771 BC); Jotham judged the people meanwhile. Thiele: 792-740 BC (coregent from 792).

events.role: King of Judah in whose days he prophesied
King whose death dates the vision

people.name: Amos
people.description: Shepherd-prophet from Tekoa who denounced social injustice in Israel.
people.dateNotes: Prophesied in the days of Uzziah (810-758) and Jeroboam II (825-784), two years before the earthquake (Amos 1:1): between 810 and 784 BC on Ussher's chain, c. 760 BC in modern reckoning. Birth and death estimated (death c. 740 BC).

people.name: Zechariah of Israel
people.description: King of Israel, son of Jeroboam II and the last of Jehu's dynasty, who reigned six months before Shallum son of Jabesh killed him before the people. His fall fulfilled the word that Jehu's sons would sit on the throne to the fourth generation (2 Kgs 15:8-12; 10:30).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned six months in 773-772 BC, from the 38th year of Azariah (2 Kgs 15:8), after an interregnum following Jeroboam II's death. Thiele: 753 BC. Birth estimated. Not the prophet Zechariah.

people.name: Jeiel the scribe
people.description: Scribe who mustered Uzziah's army.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Maaseiah the ruler under Uzziah
people.description: Officer who mustered Uzziah's army with Jeiel.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Hananiah, captain of Uzziah
people.description: One of the king's captains over whom the army of Uzziah was ordered.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Shallum of Israel
people.description: Usurper who killed Zechariah son of Jeroboam II and reigned over Israel a full month in Samaria, until Menahem son of Gadi came up from Tirzah and killed him (2 Kgs 15:10-15).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: one month in 772 BC, in the 39th year of Uzziah (2 Kgs 15:13). Thiele: 752 BC. Birth estimated. Not Shallum (Jehoahaz) of Judah.

people.name: Menahem
people.description: King of Israel for ten years who seized the throne by killing Shallum and brutally sacked Tiphsah (2 Kgs 15:14-16). He paid Pul king of Assyria a thousand talents of silver, raised from Israel's wealthy men, to secure his kingdom (2 Kgs 15:19-20).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 772-761 BC (ten years from the 39th year of Azariah, 2 Kgs 15:17; Pekahiah succeeded in Azariah's 50th, 15:23). Thiele: 752-742 BC; Assyrian records list Menahem of Samaria among Tiglath-pileser III's tributaries c. 738 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Zadok, father of Jerusha
people.description: Father of Jerusha, mother of King Jotham; not Zadok the priest.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Hosea
people.description: Prophet who married Gomer to illustrate God's love for unfaithful Israel.
people.dateNotes: Prophesied in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah of Judah and of Jeroboam II of Israel (Hos 1:1): on Ussher's chain from before 784 BC into Hezekiah's reign (from 726 BC). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Zechariah, father of Abi
people.description: Father of Abi, mother of Hezekiah (also called Abijah in Chronicles).
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Rezin
people.description: King of Syria (Aram) from Damascus who, with Pekah of Israel, marched against Ahaz of Judah. Isaiah told Ahaz not to fear these two "smoking firebrands." Rezin recovered Elath for Syria; Tiglath-pileser of Assyria then took Damascus and killed him.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. He fought Ahaz in the Syro-Ephraimite war (about 742 BC) and was killed when Tiglath-pileser took Damascus (2 Kgs 16:9), dated here to 740 BC. Birth is an estimate.

events.role: King of Syria who besieged Jerusalem with Pekah

people.name: Pekahiah
people.description: King of Israel, son of Menahem, who reigned two years before Pekah son of Remaliah, one of his captains, killed him in the palace at Samaria (2 Kgs 15:23-26).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 761-759 BC, from the 50th year of Azariah (2 Kgs 15:23). Thiele: 742-740 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Baladan, father of Merodach-baladan
people.description: Father of Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

scripture.context: Father of the king of Babylon

people.name: Isaiah
people.description: Jerusalem prophet who saw the Lord enthroned in the temple and counseled kings Ahaz and Hezekiah through the Assyrian crisis. His visions of Immanuel and the suffering servant shaped messianic hope, and the great Isaiah scroll from Qumran is the best preserved of the Dead Sea Scrolls.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §583-584: called in 759 BC, the year Uzziah died (Isa 6:1); the Annals (§553) also place him in Judah under Uzziah, earlier. Tradition: martyred by Manasseh c. 695 BC (cf. Heb 11:37; Annals §682). Isa 37:38 reports Sennacherib's death, which Assyrian records date to 681 BC, so either Isaiah outlived 695 or the notice was added later. Born c. 783 BC (estimated; Ussher gives no birth year).

people.name: Pekah
people.description: King of Israel, son of Remaliah, who killed Pekahiah and allied with Rezin of Aram against Ahaz of Judah (2 Kgs 16:5; Isa 7:1-9). In his days Tiglath-pileser took Galilee and Gilead and carried their people captive, and Hoshea son of Elah conspired against him and killed him (2 Kgs 15:29-30).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 759-739 BC (20 years from the 52nd year of Azariah, 2 Kgs 15:27, 15:32); Ahaz began at the end of his 17th year (2 Kgs 16:1; Annals §597). He was killed by Hoshea in the 20th year of Jotham (2 Kgs 15:30), counted from Jotham's first year in 759, which is 739 BC and the 4th year of Ahaz (§610). Hoshea's peaceful reign counts from the 12th year of Ahaz (730 BC, 2 Kgs 17:1), after nine years of anarchy. Thiele: 752-732 BC (partly overlapping); Assyrian records place his fall c. 732 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Tiglath-Pileser III

people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §596: began to reign in 747 BC as "Ninus the younger" (19 years, Castor); §604, §607: took Damascus and Galilee in 740 BC, the 3rd year of Ahaz; §615: died in 728 BC and was succeeded by Shalmaneser. Ussher keeps Pul apart from him: Pul took Menahem's tribute in 771 BC (2 Kgs 15:19-20; §574-576), and 1 Chr 5:26 names the two kings separately. Birth unknown (estimate). Mainstream: Pul and Tiglath-pileser are one king, reigned 745-727 BC.

people.dateNotes: Ussher: killed Pekah in the 20th year of Jotham, 739 BC (2 Kgs 15:30; Annals §610), then reigned 9 years from the 12th year of Ahaz, 730 BC (2 Kgs 17:1; §614), after nine years of anarchy; Hezekiah began in his 3rd year (2 Kgs 18:1) and Samaria fell in his 9th, 721 BC, Hezekiah's 6th (2 Kgs 18:10; §633). Imprisoned by the king of Assyria (17:4); his death is unrecorded, so the death year is approximate. Thiele: 732-723 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Ahaz
people.description: Wicked king of Judah who practiced child sacrifice and shut the Temple doors.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §597: reigned 742-726 BC (16 years, 2 Kgs 16:1-2), from the 17th year of Pekah. §579: born 762 BC (age 20 at accession). Taken as written, the figures make Ahaz about 10 at the birth of Hezekiah (born 752 BC, §586; Ussher himself counts 11 and cites Tremellius, who read the 20 years as Jotham's accession rather than Ahaz's); the text is kept and the difficulty is unresolved. Thiele: 732-715 BC. Isaiah 7.

people.name: Hezekiah
people.description: A reforming king of Judah who purged idolatry and trusted God when Sennacherib's Assyrian army besieged Jerusalem. His water tunnel from the Gihon spring survives, and the Siloam inscription found in it in 1880 records his workmen's feat, corroborating the biblical account.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §586: born 752 BC to Ahaz and Abi, daughter of Zachariah; 25 at accession (2 Kgs 18:2). §617, §620: made viceroy in Ahaz's last year (727) and reigned alone from 726; 29 years, to 698 BC (§682). Samaria fell in his sixth year (721 BC, §633) and Sennacherib came in his fourteenth (713 BC, §642, §645), after which fifteen years were added to his life (2 Kgs 20:6). By these figures Ahaz was about 10 at Hezekiah's birth (§579). Thiele and most modern scholars: 715-686 BC, with Sennacherib's invasion in 701 BC.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.description: The weeping prophet who warned Judah for decades of coming Babylonian judgment, endured imprisonment and a muddy cistern, and promised a new covenant written on the heart. Clay bullae from the City of David bear names of royal officials, such as Jehucal son of Shelemiah, who appear in his book.
people.dateNotes: Called in the 13th year of Josiah (Jer 1:2), 629 BC on Ussher's chain (Annals §737; 627 in modern reckoning), while still a youth (1:6); active to the fall of Jerusalem and afterwards in Egypt (Jer 43-44). Birth and death estimated; tradition says he was stoned in Egypt.

people.name: Habakkuk
people.description: Prophet who questioned God about evil and received answers about faith.
people.dateNotes: The book foresees the rise of the Chaldeans (Hab 1:6) and is usually dated c. 610-600 BC, late in Josiah's reign or under Jehoiakim; it names no king. Contemporary of Jeremiah. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Pashur son of Immer

people.dateNotes: Estimate. He was chief governor of the temple during Jeremiah's ministry (Jer 20:1-6), which this timeline starts in 629 BC. The year of the incident is not given and his death is not recorded.

people.name: Ashpenaz
people.description: Chief of Nebuchadnezzar's eunuchs, ordered to bring young Israelites of the royal family and nobility to be trained in Babylonian language and learning. He gave Daniel and his three friends their Babylonian names and showed them favour when Daniel asked to avoid the king's food.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Active when Daniel was taken to Babylon in 607 BC (Dan 1:3). His death is not recorded.

people.name: Arioch

people.dateNotes: Estimate. Active at the time of Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the statue, 604 BC (Dan 2:14-25). His death is not recorded.

events.role: Sent to execute the wise men; brought Daniel to the king

people.dateNotes: Estimate from the period of the text; no birth year recorded.

people.name: Josiah
people.description: Judah's young king whose temple repairs uncovered the book of the law, igniting the kingdom's most sweeping religious reform. He centralized worship in Jerusalem, renewed the covenant, and kept a Passover unmatched since the judges; scholars link his lawbook to Deuteronomy.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 641-610 BC (31 years, 2 Kgs 22:1). Age 8 at accession: born 649 BC, when Amon was about 16; the text's figures also make Josiah about 14 at the birth of Jehoiakim (25 in 610, 2 Kgs 23:36). Killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necho (2 Kgs 23:29). Thiele and modern scholarship: 640-609 BC.

events.role: King in whose days he was called

people.name: Hananiah son of Azur
people.description: False prophet from Gibeon who told the people in the temple that Babylon's yoke would be broken within two years. He broke the wooden yoke Jeremiah wore. Jeremiah answered that the LORD had not sent him, and he died that same year.
people.dateNotes: He spoke in the fourth year of Zedekiah and died the same year, in the seventh month (Jer 28:1, 17); Ussher dates this to 597 BC. Birth is an estimate. Not the Hananiah who is Shadrach.

people.name: Baruch son of Neriah
people.description: Jeremiah's scribe and companion. He wrote down Jeremiah's prophecies from dictation, read them publicly in the temple, witnessed the purchase of the field at Anathoth, and was taken with Jeremiah to Egypt. The LORD gave him a personal word in Jeremiah 45.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. He was a grown man writing for Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim (Jer 36:1-4) and still with him in Egypt after 588 BC (Jer 43:6). His death is not recorded; later traditions about it are not in Scripture.

people.dateNotes: Estimate. He acted on the seventh day of the fifth month of Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year, 588 BC (2 Kgs 25:8). His death is not recorded.

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.description: The Babylonian king who besieged Jerusalem, destroyed Solomon's temple, and carried Judah into exile, yet appears in Daniel as a ruler humbled to confess the Most High. The Babylonian Chronicle preserves his own court's terse record of the first capture of the city.
people.dateNotes: Scripture ties his reign to the kings of Judah: his 1st year is Jehoiakim's 4th (Jer 25:1; Dan 1:1), the 18th is Zedekiah's 10th (Jer 32:1), Jehoiachin was taken in his 8th (2 Kgs 24:12) and Jerusalem burned in his 19th (2 Kgs 25:8). Ussher, Annals §768-782, 890: viceroy from 607 BC (20 months), sole king from 605 on his father's death, died 562 BC after 43 years alone. Mainstream: reigned 605-562 BC (Babylonian Chronicle), with the fall of Jerusalem in 587/586. Birth estimated (c. 634-630 BC).

people.name: Jehoahaz of Judah
people.description: Son of Josiah, made king by the people of the land at 23 after his father fell at Megiddo. He reigned three months before Pharaoh Necho bound him at Riblah and took him to Egypt, where he died (2 Kgs 23:30-34; Jer 22:10-12).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned three months in 610 BC (2 Kgs 23:31); age 23 at accession, so born 633 BC. Modern scholarship: 609 BC. Called Shallum in Jer 22:11 and 1 Chr 3:15. Died in Egypt at an unrecorded date. Not Jehoahaz of Israel; Ahaziah of Judah is also called Jehoahaz (2 Chr 21:17).

people.name: Gemariah, son of Hilkiah

people.description: Son of Ahikam and grandson of Shaphan. After Jerusalem fell, Nebuchadnezzar made him governor over the people left in the land, at Mizpah. Jeremiah lived under his protection. He ignored warnings of a plot and was murdered by Ishmael son of Nethaniah, after which the remnant fled to Egypt.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Appointed after the fall of Jerusalem and killed in the seventh month (2 Kgs 25:22-25); Ussher dates both in 588 BC, the same year. Birth is an estimate from his father's career.

people.name: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian

people.dateNotes: Estimate. Active when Jeremiah was in the cistern, 589 BC in this timeline (Jer 38:7-13). His death is not recorded.

people.name: Ezekiel
people.description: Priest deported to Babylon who received his prophetic call amid visions of the divine chariot beside the Chebar canal. Through stark symbolic acts he interpreted Jerusalem's fall and foresaw dry bones living and a new temple; cuneiform records of Judean exile settlements corroborate his community's setting.
people.dateNotes: Taken to Babylon with Jehoiachin (2 Kgs 24:14-16), 599 BC on Ussher's chain (597 modern; Annals §796). Called on 24 July 595 BC, in the fifth year of that captivity (Ezek 1:2; Annals §821). Ussher reads the thirtieth year of 1:1 as thirty years from Josiah's reform of 624 BC; others read it as Ezekiel's age. Last dated oracle in the 27th year (29:17), c. 573 BC. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Ishmael son of Nethaniah

people.name: Daniel
people.description: A Judean noble exiled to Babylon who rose to high office under Babylonian and Persian rulers while refusing to compromise his devotion to God. His deliverance from the lions' den and his sweeping visions of successive empires shaped Jewish and Christian hope in God's coming kingdom.
people.dateNotes: Deported as a youth in the 4th year of Jehoiakim by Ussher's count (Dan 1:1-6), 607 BC (Annals §776; 605 modern). His last dated vision is in the third year of Cyrus (Dan 10:1), 535 BC counting from the edict of 537 (Annals §956; 536 BC in modern reckoning); Ussher puts his death shortly after, which is left unrecorded here. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Zedekiah
people.description: Last king of Judah; blinded and taken captive to Babylon.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 599-588 BC (11 years, 2 Kgs 24:18). Age 21 at accession: born 620 BC. Blinded and taken to Babylon when Jerusalem fell in 588 BC; he died in prison there at an unrecorded date (Jer 52:11), so the death year is approximate. Modern scholarship: 597-587/586 BC.

events.role: King who yielded to the officials

people.dateNotes: Usually dated soon after the fall of Jerusalem (Obad 11-14), 588 BC on Ussher's chain (587/586 in modern reckoning); some date the book to Edom's revolt under Jehoram of Judah (2 Kgs 8:20-22). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Shadrach
people.description: One of Daniel's three companions who survived the fiery furnace.
people.dateNotes: Dan 1:6-7; 3:1-30. Deported with Daniel in 607 BC on Ussher's reckoning (Annals §776). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Meshach

people.name: Abednego

people.name: Neri
people.description: Named in Luke 3:27 as the son of Melchi and father of Shealtiel, the point where Luke's line through Nathan touches the royal line of Matthew. Matthew 1:12 and 1 Chronicles 3:17 make Shealtiel a son of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah), so the lists disagree. Two classic explanations are offered. One treats it as a levirate or adoptive link, Shealtiel becoming heir to Neri's line when Jehoiachin was recorded as childless (Jer 22:30). The other holds that Luke traces Mary's ancestry, in which Neri is her forebear and the name Shealtiel belongs to a separate line or a shared name. This table keeps Matthew's father for Shealtiel and shows Neri as a parent relationship.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Luke's genealogy. Luke identifies Shealtiel as son of Neri rather than Jeconiah (Matt 1:12).

people.name: Pharaoh Hophra
people.description: King of Egypt whom Jeremiah said would be given to his enemies; the Apries of Greek sources.

people.name: Jehoiachin
people.description: Son of Jehoiakim; king of Judah for 3 months. Deported to Babylon; later released by Evil-Merodach. In the lineage of Jesus.
people.dateNotes: 2 Kgs 24:8-16; 25:27-30; Jer 22:24-30; Matt 1:11-12. Ussher: reigned three months in 599 BC, then deported (Annals §794-796); released by Evil-merodach in the 37th year of his captivity (2 Kgs 25:27), 562 BC (§891). Age 18 at accession (2 Kgs 24:8): born 617 BC; 2 Chr 36:9 reads 8. The Babylonian Chronicle dates his surrender to March 597 BC. Ussher thinks he died about 560 BC, when Evil-merodach did (§899); the year is an estimate.

events.role: Exiled king whose captivity dates it

people.name: Darius the Mede
people.description: Ruler called Darius the Median who received the kingdom of Babylon at about 62 after Belshazzar's death (Dan 5:31). Pressed by his officials, he had Daniel thrown to the lions and then honored Daniel's God when he was delivered (Dan 6). He is not named outside Daniel and his identity is debated.
people.dateNotes: Dan 5:31; 6:1-28; 9:1; 11:1. Ussher, Annals §792, 939, 948: Cyaxares, son of Astyages (Ahasuerus of Dan 9:1), born 601 BC and 62 years old when he took the kingdom on Babylon's fall in 538 BC; he reigned two years, and Cyrus's first year followed in 537 BC. Death unrecorded. Mainstream: Babylon fell in 539 BC, and he is variously identified with Gubaru/Ugbaru, Cyaxares II or Cyrus himself; distinct from Darius I (522-486 BC).

people.name: Cyrus
people.description: Founder of the Persian Empire who took Babylon and permitted Judah's exiles to return and rebuild the temple. Isaiah strikingly names this Gentile king the Lord's anointed, and the Cyrus Cylinder documents his wider policy of restoring displaced peoples and their sanctuaries.
people.dateNotes: Isa 44:28; 45:1; 2 Chr 36:22-23; Ezra 1:1-4. Took Babylon in October 539 BC and died in 530 BC. Ussher dates his decree (Ezra 1:1) to 537 BC (Annals §948-949), counting his first year after Darius the Mede; modern scholarship gives 538 BC. Birth estimated.

events.role: King whose decree released the exiles

people.name: Shealtiel

Luke 3:27 calls him the son of Neri, so the genealogies differ here. Two classic explanations are offered. One holds that Shealtiel was Jehoiachin's son by birth and Neri's heir by levirate or adoptive succession, Jehoiachin being recorded as childless in Jer 22:30. The other holds that Luke follows Mary's line, in which Neri is her ancestor. This table follows Matthew for his father and shows Neri as a parent relationship. He lived in the exile in Babylon.
people.dateNotes: Exilic period. Born in Babylon after Jeconiah's deportation, 599 BC on Ussher's chain (597 BC by the Babylonian Chronicle; 1 Chr 3:17). Birth estimated.

people.name: Belshazzar

people.dateNotes: Esth 3-7. Executed in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus (Esth 3:7; 7:10), 474/473 BC if he is Xerxes I. Birth estimated.

people.dateNotes: Estimate. The plot came soon after Esther was made queen in the seventh year (Esth 2:16, 21-23). Death date approximate. The record of it is read to the king years later (Esth 6:2).
