events.description: William Tyndale published the first printed English New Testament, translated directly from Erasmus' Greek text and smuggled into England in bales of cloth. Though Tyndale was later executed, his vivid phrasing endured, shaping much of the King James New Testament's wording.
events.dateNotes: Printing began in Cologne in 1525 but was stopped by the authorities; the first complete printed English New Testament appeared at Worms in 1526. Tyndale was executed in 1536.

events.name: Calvin Publishes Institutes of the Christian Religion
events.description: John Calvin publishes the first edition of the Institutes in Basel at age 26, expanded in later editions to the definitive 1559 Latin text, which became a foundational statement of Reformed theology.
events.dateNotes: First edition 1536; expanded final edition 1559.

events.name: William Tyndale Executed
events.description: Tyndale is strangled and burned at Vilvoorde near Brussels in October 1536 for translating the Bible into English. His wording largely shaped the King James Version.
events.dateNotes: Early October 1536; the exact day is unknown.

events.name: Ignatius Founds the Jesuits
events.description: Pope Paul III approves the Society of Jesus on 27 September 1540. Founded by Ignatius of Loyola and his companions, it centres on education, missions and obedience to the pope and becomes a major force in Catholic renewal and world missions.
events.dateNotes: Bull Regimini militantis ecclesiae, 27 September 1540.

events.name: Council of Trent
events.description: Meeting in three periods between 1545 and 1563, the Council of Trent defined Catholic doctrine on Scripture, justification and the sacraments, and enacted reforms of clergy and discipline in response to Protestant challenges.
events.dateNotes: Council of Trent, 1545–1563 (three periods over 18 years).

events.name: Francis Xavier Reaches Japan
events.description: Francis Xavier, a Jesuit co-founder, lands at Kagoshima on 15 August 1549 and begins the first Christian mission in Japan. After two years he leaves a small community that grows into one of the largest in Asia before later persecution.
events.dateNotes: Landed 15 August 1549; left Japan in 1551.

events.name: Valladolid Debate on the Indies
events.description: At Charles Vs order, Bartolome de las Casas and Juan Gines de Sepulveda argue before a council of theologians whether Spain may wage war on the native peoples. The judges gave no formal verdict and both sides claimed success, but Las Casass defence of Native Americans dignity became a landmark.
events.dateNotes: Sessions August-September 1550 and April-May 1551.

events.name: Scottish Reformation
events.description: The Scottish Parliament meeting at Edinburgh in August 1560 abolishes papal authority and the Mass and adopts the Scots Confession, drafted by John Knox and five others. The Church of Scotland takes a Reformed, Presbyterian course.
events.dateNotes: Reformation Parliament, 1-27 August 1560.

people.role: Chief author of the Confession and preacher

events.name: King James Version Published
events.description: Commissioned by James I after the Hampton Court Conference (1604), about fifty scholars in six companies at Westminster, Oxford and Cambridge produced a new English Bible from the Hebrew and Greek. Building heavily on Tyndale, the King James Version became among the most influential books in the English language.
events.dateNotes: Published 1611.

people.role: Translator and head of a translation company

events.name: Westminster Confession of Faith
events.description: The Westminster Assembly (1643-1653) produces a Reformed confession, completed in 1646, that became the standard of English-speaking Presbyterian churches and shaped Congregational and Baptist confessions.
events.dateNotes: The Assembly first met in 1643; the Confession was completed in 1646 and adopted by the Church of Scotland (1647); the English Parliament approved most of it in 1648.

events.name: Peace of Westphalia
events.description: The treaties ending the Thirty Years' War confirm the settlement of the Peace of Augsburg (1555) and extend its toleration to the Reformed church, ending a long period of European religious wars. The principle of cuius regio, eius religio dates from Augsburg, not 1648.
events.dateNotes: Treaties signed October 24, 1648.

events.name: Pilgrims Progress Published
events.description: John Bunyan publishes the first part of The Pilgrims Progress, an allegory of the Christian life. It is written in plain English from the Bible and has been translated into over two hundred languages.
events.dateNotes: Part 1 published 1678; Part 2 in 1684. Composition during imprisonment at Bedford is likely but debated.

events.name: Rescue from the Epworth Rectory Fire
events.description: On 9 February 1709 the rectory at Epworth burns down, and five-year-old John Wesley is pulled from an upstairs window. Susanna Wesley, who taught her children at home, saw it as Gods special care for him, and Wesley later called himself a brand plucked from the burning.
events.dateNotes: 9 February 1709.

events.name: The Holy Club at Oxford
events.description: Charles Wesley and friends meet at Oxford for study, prayer, Communion and visiting prisoners. John Wesley soon leads the group, and its disciplined method earns the nickname Methodists. George Whitefield joins a few years later.
events.dateNotes: Begun 1729; John Wesley took the lead later that year; members dispersed after 1735.

events.name: Jonathan Edwards and the First Great Awakening
events.description: Revival in Jonathan Edwards' Northampton church (1734-35) and George Whitefield's preaching tours from 1739 spread the First Great Awakening through the American colonies, alongside the Evangelical Revival in Britain. Edwards' sermon "Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God" (1741) became its best-known sermon.
events.dateNotes: First Great Awakening, c. 1734–1743.

events.name: John Wesley's Aldersgate Experience
events.description: Wesley feels his heart "strangely warmed" at a Moravian society meeting on Aldersgate Street, an experience he treated as a turning point in his own assurance of faith and that is often seen as the spiritual birth of the Methodist revival.

people.role: Mother whose teaching shaped the Wesleys
Brother; his own evangelical conversion came three days earlier

events.name: William Carey Sails for India
events.description: The Baptist missionary William Carey sails from England on 13 June 1793 and reaches Calcutta in November, beginning a lifelong work of Bible translation, education and social reform; he is often called the "father of modern missions".
events.dateNotes: Carey departed June 13, 1793; established Serampore Mission.

events.name: British and Foreign Bible Society Founded
events.description: The British and Foreign Bible Society is founded in London to make the Scriptures available in every language, becoming the model for Bible societies around the world.
events.dateNotes: Founded March 7, 1804.

people.role: Welsh Methodist whose Bible appeal led to its founding

events.name: Slave Trade Abolished in the British Empire
events.description: Parliament passes the Slave Trade Act on 25 March 1807 after twenty years of campaigning led by William Wilberforce and many others, especially evangelical Christians and Quakers. Slavery itself was abolished across the empire in 1833, days before Wilberforce died.
events.dateNotes: Royal Assent 25 March 1807; Slavery Abolition Act 1833.

events.name: American Bible Society Founded
events.description: Founded to distribute Bibles across the expanding American frontier.
events.dateNotes: Founded May 11, 1816 in New York.

events.name: Charles Spurgeon Begins Preaching in London
events.description: Spurgeon, the "Prince of Preachers," begins pastoring at New Park Street Chapel at age 19; his later Metropolitan Tabernacle seats about 5,000.
events.dateNotes: Spurgeon preached to millions over 38 years (1854–1892).

events.name: Samuel Ajayi Crowther Consecrated Bishop
events.description: Crowther, born in Yorubaland, enslaved as a boy, rescued by the Royal Navy and educated in Sierra Leone, is consecrated at Canterbury Cathedral on 29 June 1864. He is the first African Anglican bishop and oversees the Niger mission. He also translated the Bible into Yoruba.

events.name: Hudson Taylor Founds the China Inland Mission
events.description: Hudson Taylor founds the China Inland Mission in 1865 to carry the gospel to Chinas inland provinces. It is non-denominational and depends on prayer rather than appeals for funds, and by 1900 it is the largest mission in China.
events.dateNotes: Founded in June 1865.

events.name: D.L. Moody's Revival Campaigns
events.description: Dwight L. Moody's transatlantic revival campaigns in Britain and America bring millions to evangelistic meetings. He founds Moody Bible Institute (1886).
events.dateNotes: Major campaigns: Britain (1873–75), America (1875–99).

events.name: Azusa Street Revival
events.description: William Seymour leads a multiracial revival on Azusa Street in Los Angeles, a major catalyst of the global Pentecostal movement, which with the charismatic movements now numbers hundreds of millions.
events.dateNotes: Azusa Street Revival, 312 Azusa Street, April 1906 – c. 1909.

events.name: Edinburgh Missionary Conference
events.description: The World Missionary Conference in Edinburgh brings together about 1,200 delegates, mostly from Protestant and Anglican societies, and is widely seen as a starting point of the modern ecumenical movement.

events.name: Barmen Declaration
events.description: Meeting at Barmen, the Confessing Church in Germany adopts a declaration, drafted chiefly by Karl Barth with the Lutheran Hans Asmussen and Thomas Breit, rejecting Nazi ideology's claims over the church. Bonhoeffer and Martin Niemoller supported the Confessing movement but were not its authors.
events.dateNotes: Barmen Declaration, May 31, 1934.

people.role: Supporter of the Confessing movement (not an author of the Declaration)

events.name: C. S. Lewis Broadcasts on the BBC
events.description: During the Second World War Lewis gives radio talks on Christian belief on the BBC. They are published as separate books and in 1952 as Mere Christianity, a widely read defence of Christianity across denominations.
events.dateNotes: Talks 1941-1944; collected as Mere Christianity in 1952.

events.name: Bonhoeffer Executed at Flossenburg
events.description: Dietrich Bonhoeffer, a pastor in the Confessing Church who joined the plot against Hitler, is hanged on 9 April 1945, a month before the war ended. His Cost of Discipleship and Letters and Papers from Prison remain widely read.
events.dateNotes: 9 April 1945.

events.name: Discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls
events.description: A Bedouin shepherd's find in a cave near Qumran in 1946-47 opened one of the greatest manuscript finds of modern times: some 900 scrolls from eleven caves, usually linked to a Jewish community at Qumran, often identified as Essene. Every Hebrew Bible book except Esther is represented, and the Great Isaiah Scroll predates the earlier known Hebrew manuscripts by about a thousand years.
events.dateNotes: First scrolls found in 1946-47; excavations continued through 1956.

people.role: Acquired scrolls for the Hebrew University
Photographed and helped date the Isaiah scroll
Shepherd who found the first scrolls

events.name: State of Israel Established
events.description: As the British Mandate ended, David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the State of Israel, the first sovereign Jewish state in the land since antiquity. The ingathering of Jewish exiles and the revival of Hebrew as a living national language gave the ancient biblical homeland renewed centrality in Jewish life and Christian reflection.

people.role: Declared the state; first prime minister

events.name: Billy Graham's Global Crusades
events.description: Graham preached the gospel in person to an estimated 215 million people in more than 185 countries over a career of some five decades, according to the Billy Graham Evangelistic Association.
events.dateNotes: Los Angeles Crusade (1949) launched Graham's global ministry.

events.name: Mother Teresa Founds the Missionaries of Charity
events.description: On 7 October 1950 the diocese of Calcutta approves Mother Teresas new order, which serves the dying and destitute. It grows into thousands of sisters in over a hundred countries.
events.dateNotes: Approved 7 October 1950.

events.name: Second Vatican Council
events.description: Pope John XXIII convenes Vatican II, transforming Catholic worship (Mass in the vernacular), affirming religious liberty, and opening dialogue with Protestants and other faiths.
events.dateNotes: Vatican II, October 11, 1962 – December 8, 1965.

people.role: Pope who continued and closed the council

events.name: Letter from Birmingham Jail
events.description: Imprisoned for protesting segregation, Martin Luther King Jr. writes an open letter on 16 April 1963 to white clergy who had urged him to wait. He appeals to Scripture, Augustine and Aquinas to explain why unjust laws must be resisted nonviolently.
events.dateNotes: Written 16 April 1963.

events.name: Lausanne Congress on World Evangelization
events.description: Billy Graham convenes about 2,700 evangelical leaders and guests from some 150 nations; the resulting Lausanne Covenant, drafted under John Stott, shapes evangelical mission for a generation.
events.dateNotes: July 16–25, 1974, Lausanne, Switzerland.

events.name: Christianity Shifts to the Global South
events.description: Between about 1980 and 2000 the center of gravity of world Christianity moved: the majority of Christians came to live in Africa, Asia and Latin America rather than in Europe and North America.
events.dateNotes: Estimates of when the crossover occurred vary with the counting method; see Philip Jenkins, The Next Christendom (2002), and Pew Research Center data.

events.name: Fall of the Soviet Union
events.description: The dissolution of the USSR on 26 December 1991 ends some seven decades of official state atheism and opens the former Soviet republics to far greater religious freedom, with a revival of Orthodox and other churches.
events.dateNotes: December 26, 1991.

locations.name: Eden
locations.description: Garden where God placed Adam and Eve (Gen 2:8-14). Its location is unknown: Genesis names four rivers, including the Tigris and Euphrates, and proposals range from southern Mesopotamia to Armenia; the world before the Flood may no longer exist. No coordinates are given.

locations.name: Ur
locations.description: Home city of Abraham's family, "Ur of the Chaldees" (Gen 11:28, 31; Acts 7:2-4), traditionally Tell el-Muqayyar in southern Iraq. Some scholars propose a northern Ur near Haran; the southern site is the majority identification.

locations.name: Haran
locations.description: Where Abraham's family settled before Canaan.

locations.name: Canaan
locations.description: The land west of the Jordan promised to Abraham (Gen 12:7; 17:8). The map pin marks the middle of the region, not a city.

locations.name: Egypt
locations.description: Where Israel settled under Joseph and was later enslaved. Scripture gives 430 years for the sojourn of Israel (Exod 12:40-41) and 400 years of affliction (Gen 15:13; Acts 7:6). On Ussher's chronology the 430 years run from Abraham's call in 1921 BC to the Exodus in 1491 BC, with about 215 years spent in Egypt (from 1706 BC). The pin is a centre-of-country marker.

locations.name: Mount Sinai
locations.description: Where God gave Moses the Law (Exod 19-20). Jebel Musa in the southern Sinai is the traditional identification (from about the 4th century AD); other proposals include Jebel Sin Bisher, Har Karkom and Jebel al-Lawz in Arabia (Midian). The site is not certain.

locations.name: Jerusalem
locations.description: City of David; location of the Temple.

locations.name: Bethlehem
locations.description: Birthplace of David and Jesus.

locations.name: Babylon
locations.description: Capital of Babylonian Empire; place of exile.

locations.name: Nazareth
locations.description: Hometown of Jesus.

locations.name: Capernaum
locations.description: Base of Jesus' Galilean ministry.

locations.name: Damascus
locations.description: Where Paul was converted.

locations.name: Antioch
locations.description: Center of early Gentile Christianity.

locations.name: Rome
locations.description: Capital of the Roman Empire; center of early church.

locations.name: Patmos
locations.description: Island where John wrote Revelation.

locations.name: Cana
locations.description: Galilean village where Jesus turned water into wine (John 2:1-11). Kafr Kanna is the traditional site; Khirbet Qana, about 13 km north of Nazareth, is a leading alternative.

locations.name: Sea of Galilee
locations.description: Lake where Jesus calmed the storm and walked on water.

locations.name: Bethsaida
locations.description: Fishing village on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee; home of Peter, Andrew and Philip (John 1:44). Et-Tell is the usual identification; el-Araj is a proposed alternative.

locations.name: Nain
locations.description: Village where Jesus raised the widow's son.

locations.name: Bethany
locations.description: Village near Jerusalem; home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus.

locations.name: Gadara
locations.description: Decapolis city whose territory Matthew places the healing of the demon-possessed man in (Matt 8:28). Mark 5:1 and Luke 8:26 read "Gerasenes" (Gerasa or Kursi) in many manuscripts, and some read "Gergesenes"; the exact site is uncertain.

locations.name: Jericho
locations.description: Ancient city near the Jordan; site of Bartimaeus' healing.

locations.name: Tyre & Sidon
locations.description: Coastal cities of Phoenicia where Jesus healed the Syrophoenician woman's daughter (Matt 15:21-28). The map pin marks Tyre; Sidon lies about 35 km to the north.

locations.name: Decapolis
locations.description: League of ten Greco-Roman cities east of the Jordan.

locations.name: Jordan River
locations.description: River where Naaman was healed and Jesus was baptized.

locations.name: Samaria
locations.description: Philip preached and performed miracles here (Acts 8).

locations.name: Gaza Road
locations.description: Desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza where Philip baptized the Ethiopian official (Acts 8:26). The map pin marks Gaza at the end of the road.

locations.name: Joppa
locations.description: Where Peter raised Tabitha and had the vision of the sheet (Acts 9-10).

locations.name: Caesarea
locations.description: Roman capital of Judea; house of Cornelius; Paul's imprisonment (Acts 10, 23-26).

locations.name: Cyprus
locations.description: Home of Barnabas; first stop on Paul's first journey (Acts 13:4-12).

locations.name: Pisidian Antioch
locations.description: Paul preached in the synagogue; many believed (Acts 13:14-52).

locations.name: Iconium
locations.description: Paul and Barnabas preached but were driven out (Acts 14:1-7).

locations.name: Lystra
locations.description: Paul healed a lame man; later stoned (Acts 14:8-20).

locations.name: Derbe
locations.description: Lycaonian city where Paul and Barnabas made many disciples (Acts 14:20-21). Kerti Hoyuk is the usual identification; Devri Sehri is another proposal.

locations.name: Troas
locations.description: Paul received the Macedonian vision (Acts 16:8-10).

locations.name: Philippi
locations.description: First European church; Lydia converted; Paul imprisoned (Acts 16:11-40).

locations.name: Thessalonica
locations.description: Paul preached in synagogue; accused of sedition (Acts 17:1-9).

locations.name: Berea
locations.description: Bereans examined Scriptures daily to verify Paul's teaching (Acts 17:10-15).

locations.name: Athens
locations.description: Paul preached on the Areopagus about the Unknown God (Acts 17:16-34).

locations.name: Corinth
locations.description: Paul stayed 18 months; Gallio tribunal (Acts 18:1-17).

locations.name: Ephesus
locations.description: Paul taught 2 years; riot of Demetrius the silversmith (Acts 19).

locations.name: Miletus
locations.description: Paul's farewell to Ephesian elders (Acts 20:17-38).

locations.name: Crete
locations.description: Mediterranean island where Paul's ship put in at Fair Havens (Acts 27:7-12). The map pin marks the middle of the island.

locations.name: Malta
locations.description: Paul shipwrecked; healed the sick (Acts 27:39–28:10).

locations.name: Puteoli
locations.description: Port where Paul landed in Italy (Acts 28:13).

locations.name: Shechem
locations.description: Abraham built an altar here; Jacob bought land. First stop in Canaan.

locations.name: Hebron
locations.description: Abraham settled at the oaks of Mamre; burial site of the patriarchs.

locations.name: Beersheba
locations.description: Well of the oath between Abraham and Abimelech; Isaac and Jacob lived here.

locations.name: Goshen
locations.description: Region in eastern Egypt where Israel settled (Gen 45-47).

locations.name: Peniel
locations.description: Where Jacob wrestled with God and was renamed Israel (Gen 32:22-32).

locations.name: Red Sea Crossing
locations.modernName: Head of the Gulf of Suez (traditional area; site unknown)
locations.description: Where Israel crossed the "sea" (Hebrew yam suph, "sea of reeds"; Exod 14). The exact place is unknown. Proposals include the head of the Gulf of Suez (the traditional area, shown here), the Bitter Lakes and Lake Timsah, Lake Sirbonis on the Mediterranean coast, and the Gulf of Aqaba.

locations.name: Marah
locations.description: Bitter waters made sweet by Moses (Exod 15:23-25). Ain Hawarah is the traditional identification and is uncertain.

locations.name: Elim
locations.description: Oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees (Exod 15:27). Wadi Gharandel is the traditional identification and is uncertain.

locations.name: Rephidim
locations.description: Where God gave water from the rock and Israel fought Amalek (Exod 17). Wadi Feiran is the traditional identification; other sites are proposed.

locations.name: Kadesh Barnea
locations.description: Israel camped before entering Canaan; spies sent out (Num 13-14).

locations.name: Nineveh
locations.description: Capital of Assyria where Jonah preached repentance.

locations.name: Emmaus
locations.description: Village about 60 stadia (c. 11 km) from Jerusalem where the risen Jesus appeared to two disciples (Luke 24:13-35). Its site is disputed: Emmaus-Nicopolis (Latrun, shown here) fits the reading of 160 stadia found in some manuscripts; Qubeibeh, Abu Ghosh and Motza better fit the 60 stadia of most manuscripts.

locations.name: Constantinople
locations.description: Capital of the Eastern Roman Empire; seat of ecumenical patriarchate.

locations.name: Carthage
locations.description: Important early church centre; home of Tertullian and Cyprian, and where Augustine studied and taught before his conversion.

locations.name: Hippo Regius
locations.description: Bishopric of Augustine of Hippo.

locations.name: Nicaea
locations.description: Site of the First Ecumenical Council (325 AD).

locations.name: Chalcedon
locations.description: Site of the Council of Chalcedon (451 AD).

locations.name: Wittenberg
locations.description: Where Martin Luther posted the 95 Theses (1517).

locations.name: Geneva
locations.description: Center of John Calvin's Reformed tradition.

locations.name: Mainz
locations.description: Gutenberg's city; birthplace of the printing press.

locations.name: Canterbury
locations.description: Seat of the Archbishop of Canterbury; English Christianity.

locations.name: Worms
locations.description: Diet of Worms (1521); Luther's "Here I stand."

locations.name: Trent
locations.description: Council of Trent (1545–1563); Catholic Counter-Reformation.

locations.name: Aldersgate
locations.description: Site of John Wesley's evangelical conversion (1738).

locations.name: Edinburgh
locations.description: Edinburgh Missionary Conference (1910).

locations.name: Azusa Street
locations.description: Azusa Street Revival (1906); birth of Pentecostalism.

locations.name: Serampore
locations.description: William Carey's mission base; Bible translation center.

locations.name: Qumran
locations.description: Site where the Dead Sea Scrolls were discovered (1947).

locations.name: Northampton
locations.description: Jonathan Edwards and the First Great Awakening.

locations.name: Assisi
locations.description: Home of Francis of Assisi.

locations.name: Nuremberg
locations.description: Center of Reformation-era publishing and reform.

locations.name: Whitby
locations.description: Synod of Whitby (664); Celtic vs. Roman church.

locations.name: Clermont
locations.description: Council of Clermont (1095); Pope Urban II calls the First Crusade.

locations.name: Wycliffe Country
locations.description: Home of John Wycliffe; Morning Star of the Reformation.

locations.name: Bethel
locations.description: Where Abraham built an altar and where Jacob dreamed of a ladder to heaven (Gen 12:8; 28:10-22). The identification with Beitin is widely accepted.

locations.name: Dothan
locations.description: Where Joseph found his brothers and was sold to the Ishmaelite traders (Gen 37:17-28); Elisha was later here (2 Kgs 6:13).

locations.name: Mount Ararat
locations.description: "The mountains of Ararat" (Gen 8:4) where the ark came to rest; the region is Urartu. Scripture names no single peak. Agri Dagi is the traditional modern identification; others propose Cudi Dagi.

locations.name: Mediterranean Sea
locations.description: The "great sea" west of Israel (Num 34:6); Jonah's ship sailed from Joppa toward Tarshish on it (Jonah 1:3-4). The pin is a point at sea off the coast.

locations.name: Gath-hepher
locations.description: Hometown of the prophet Jonah in Zebulun (2 Kgs 14:25; Josh 19:13). Identification with Khirbet ez-Zurra or Mashhad is probable.

locations.name: Mount of Olives
locations.description: Ridge east of Jerusalem: site of Jesus' Olivet discourse and of Gethsemane, and where the disciples returned from after the Ascension (Acts 1:12). Bethany lies on its eastern slope (Luke 24:50).

locations.name: Susa
locations.description: Winter capital of the Persian kings where Esther, Mordecai and Haman lived (Esth 1:2) and where Nehemiah served (Neh 1:1).

locations.name: Caesarea Philippi
locations.description: Where Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ (Matt 16:13-20). The Transfiguration followed about a week later on a "high mountain" that the Gospels do not name.

locations.name: Mount Carmel
locations.description: Where Elijah confronted the prophets of Baal (1 Kgs 18:19-40). Muhraka, at the south-east end of the ridge, is the traditional site.

locations.name: Smyrna
locations.description: City of the church addressed in Rev 2:8-11 and the see of Polycarp.

locations.name: Tel Aviv
locations.description: Where the State of Israel was proclaimed on 14 May 1948.

locations.name: Sodom
locations.description: One of the cities of the plain destroyed by God (Gen 18-19). Its site is disputed: Bab edh-Dhra at the south-east of the Dead Sea (pinned here) and Tall el-Hammam in the northern Jordan plain are the leading proposals.

locations.name: Alexandria
locations.description: Great Hellenistic city and early Christian centre: home of Apollos (Acts 18:24), Origen and Athanasius.

locations.name: Milan
locations.description: Imperial city where the Edict of Milan was issued (AD 313) and where Ambrose was bishop.

locations.name: Constance
locations.description: Site of the Council of Constance (1414-1418), where Jan Hus was condemned and burned (1415).

locations.name: Fair Havens
locations.description: Harbour on the south coast of Crete where Paul's ship put in and Paul advised against sailing on (Acts 27:8-12).

locations.name: Basel
locations.description: Rhine city and printing centre where the first edition of Calvin's Institutes was published in 1536.

locations.name: Mount Tabor
locations.description: Isolated mountain in lower Galilee, scene of Barak's muster (Judg 4:6). Since at least the fourth century it has been the traditional site of the Transfiguration; the Gospels name only "a high mountain" (Matt 17:1), and Mount Hermon is the main alternative.

locations.name: Mount Nebo
locations.description: Mountain east of the Jordan from which Moses viewed the promised land and where he died (Deut 34:1-5).

locations.name: Mount Gilboa
locations.description: Ridge on the south-east edge of the Jezreel valley where Saul and Jonathan died fighting the Philistines (1 Sam 31:1-6).

locations.name: Valley of Elah
locations.description: Valley between Socoh and Azekah in the Judean lowlands where Israel and the Philistines faced each other and David fought Goliath (1 Sam 17:1-3).

locations.name: Mizpah of Benjamin
locations.description: Town in Benjamin where Samuel gathered Israel to repent and judged them (1 Sam 7:5-6). The identification with Tell en-Nasbeh is widely accepted.

locations.name: Shiloh
locations.description: Site of the tabernacle and the sanctuary of Eli in the time of the judges (1 Sam 1-4).

locations.name: Aphek
locations.description: Philistine staging ground at the head of the Yarkon river, where Israel was defeated and the ark taken (1 Sam 4:1-11).

locations.name: Spring of Harod
locations.description: Spring at the foot of Mount Gilboa where Gideon tested his army before attacking Midian (Judg 7:1-7); the exact spring is a traditional identification.

locations.name: Gaza
locations.description: Philistine coastal city where Samson was imprisoned and died in the temple of Dagon (Judg 16:21-30).

locations.name: Mount of Beatitudes
locations.modernName: Mount of Beatitudes, near Tabgha, Israel
locations.description: Hillside above the north-west shore of the Sea of Galilee, the traditional site of the Sermon on the Mount; Matthew says only that Jesus went up "into a mountain" (Matt 5:1).

locations.name: Ein Karem
locations.description: Village in the hill country west of Jerusalem, the traditional home of Zechariah and Elizabeth; Luke names only "a city of Juda" (Luke 1:39). Location is by tradition.

locations.name: Lyon
locations.description: Roman Lugdunum; Irenaeus was bishop of its church in the second century.

locations.name: Nicomedia
locations.description: Eastern imperial capital under Diocletian; the first edict against Christians was posted there in February 303 and the church was demolished.

locations.name: Ravenna
locations.description: Residence of the last western emperors, where Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus in 476.

locations.name: Monte Cassino
locations.description: Hilltop monastery founded by Benedict of Nursia around 529, where the Rule is traditionally said to have been written.

locations.name: Mecca
locations.description: Birthplace of Muhammad and the first centre of Islam.

locations.name: Medina
locations.description: City of the Hijra in 622 and the base from which the early Muslim conquests began.

locations.name: London
locations.description: Capital of England; place of the Westminster Assembly, the King James Version commission and the founding of the British and Foreign Bible Society.

locations.name: Munster
locations.description: One of the two Westphalian cities where the 1648 peace treaties were negotiated and signed.

locations.name: Osnabruck
locations.description: The other Westphalian city where the 1648 peace treaties were negotiated and signed.

locations.name: New York
locations.description: Where the American Bible Society was founded in 1816.

locations.name: Barmen
locations.description: District of Wuppertal where the Confessing Church synod met in May 1934 and issued the Barmen Declaration.

locations.name: Vatican City
locations.description: Seat of the papacy; St Peter's Basilica hosted the Second Vatican Council.

locations.name: Lausanne
locations.description: Host city of the 1974 International Congress on World Evangelization.

locations.name: Moscow
locations.description: Capital of the Soviet Union, where the state was dissolved in December 1991.

locations.name: Vagharshapat
locations.description: Royal city of Armenia and, by tradition, the place where Gregory the Illuminator brought King Tiridates III to faith around 301.

locations.name: Axum
locations.description: Capital of the Aksumite kingdom, whose king Ezana accepted Christianity in the fourth century.

locations.name: Chang'an
locations.description: Tang imperial capital where the Persian monk Alopen was received in 635; the Xi'an stele (781) records the mission.

locations.name: Mikulcice
locations.description: Major stronghold of Great Moravia, the realm to which Cyril and Methodius were sent in 863.

locations.name: Ai
locations.description: Canaanite city near Bethel; Israel was defeated there after Achan's sin and then took it by ambush (Josh 7-8).

locations.name: Gibeon
locations.description: Hivite city north-west of Jerusalem; its people made peace with Joshua, and Solomon sacrificed at its high place (Josh 9-10; 1 Kgs 3).

locations.name: En-gedi
locations.description: Oasis with caves on the western shore of the Dead Sea where David hid from Saul (1 Sam 24).

locations.name: Gilgal
locations.description: Israel's first camp in Canaan and a centre of Samuel's and Saul's time; the exact site is debated (Josh 4-5; 1 Sam 15).

locations.name: Plains of Moab
locations.modernName: East of the Jordan opposite Jericho
locations.description: Israel's camp east of the Jordan in the last year of Moses, where Balaam was hired to curse them (Num 22).

locations.name: Megiddo
locations.description: Fortress city guarding the pass from the coast into the Jezreel Valley; King Josiah died here.

locations.name: Ramoth-gilead
locations.description: Israelite city east of the Jordan, long contested with Aram.

locations.name: Jezreel
locations.description: Royal city of Ahab and Jezebel in the Jezreel Valley; Naboth's vineyard lay beside it.

locations.name: Zarephath
locations.description: Phoenician town near Sidon where Elijah stayed with a widow.

locations.name: Dan
locations.description: Northern border city where Jeroboam set up one of his golden calves.

locations.name: Chebar Canal
locations.description: Canal in Babylonia beside which the Judean exiles lived and Ezekiel saw his vision.

locations.name: Kir-hareseth
locations.description: Chief fortress of Moab, besieged by Israel and Judah.

locations.name: Machaerus
locations.description: Herodian hilltop fortress east of the Dead Sea. Josephus (Antiquities 18.119) names it as the prison where Herod Antipas held John the Baptist; the Gospels do not name the place.

locations.name: York
locations.description: Roman fortress city (Eboracum) where Constantine was proclaimed emperor in 306.

locations.name: Armagh
locations.description: Ecclesiastical capital of Ireland, traditionally founded by Patrick c. 444.

locations.name: Valladolid
locations.description: Castilian city where the debate over the treatment of Native Americans was held, 1550-51.

locations.name: Kagoshima
locations.description: Port in southern Japan where Francis Xavier landed in 1549.

locations.name: Epworth
locations.description: Lincolnshire town where Samuel Wesley was rector and John and Charles Wesley were raised.

locations.name: Oxford
locations.description: University town where the Wesleys formed the Holy Club.

locations.name: Kolkata
locations.description: City where Mother Teresa founded the Missionaries of Charity in 1950.

locations.name: Flossenburg
locations.description: Site of the concentration camp where Dietrich Bonhoeffer was executed in April 1945.

locations.name: Birmingham, Alabama
locations.description: Centre of the 1963 civil-rights campaign and site of Martin Luther King Jr.s imprisonment.

locations.name: Vilvoorde
locations.description: Town near Brussels where William Tyndale was executed in 1536.

locations.name: Mount Hor
locations.description: Mountain on the border of Edom where Aaron died; the traditional site is Jebel Harun near Petra, though the identification is uncertain.

locations.name: Way of the Red Sea (Arabah)
locations.modernName: Wadi Arabah, south of the Dead Sea (uncertain)
locations.description: Route south from Mount Hor toward the Red Sea to go around Edom; the exact camp where the serpents came is not known.

locations.name: Mount Ebal
locations.description: Mountain north of Shechem where Joshua built an altar and read the law; Mount Gerizim faces it to the south.

locations.name: Debir
locations.description: Hill-country city taken by Othniel; Khirbet Rabud is the usual identification, though some propose Tell Beit Mirsim.

locations.name: Ophrah of Abiezer
locations.description: Gideon's home town in Manasseh; the site is not certainly identified and the coordinates are approximate.

locations.name: Mizpah of Gilead
locations.description: Gilead town where Jephthah was recalled and made his vow; the location is uncertain and the coordinates approximate.

locations.name: Zorah
locations.description: Town of the tribe of Dan and home of Manoah and Samson.

locations.name: Timnah
locations.description: Philistine town in the Sorek valley where Samson found his wife.

locations.name: Gibeah of Saul
locations.description: Saul's hometown and royal seat (1 Sam 10:26; 15:34; 22:6), identified with Tell el-Ful on the ridge north of Jerusalem.

locations.name: Nob
locations.modernName: Uncertain; a ridge near Jerusalem such as Mount Scopus (proposed)
locations.description: Priestly town where the tabernacle stood in Saul's day and Ahimelech fed David (1 Sam 21-22); the site is uncertain, with proposals on the ridge just north-east of Jerusalem, so these coordinates are approximate.

locations.name: Gath
locations.description: Philistine city, home of Goliath and ruled by King Achish (1 Sam 17:4; 21:10; 27:2), identified with Tell es-Safi.

locations.name: Adullam
locations.description: Town and cave in the Judean lowland where David gathered his band (1 Sam 22:1), identified with Tel Adullam; the exact cave is not known.

locations.name: Keilah
locations.description: Judean town David delivered from the Philistines (1 Sam 23:1-5), identified with Khirbet Qila in the hills near Hebron.

locations.name: Ziklag
locations.modernName: Uncertain; Khirbet al-Ra'i or Tell es-Sharia (proposed)
locations.description: Town in the south given to David by Achish of Gath (1 Sam 27:6); its site is disputed between several tells in the western Negev, so these coordinates are approximate.

locations.name: Mahanaim
locations.modernName: Uncertain; Tulul edh-Dhahab or Tell Hajjaj (proposed)
locations.description: Town in Gilead east of the Jordan, Ish-bosheth's capital and David's refuge from Absalom (2 Sam 2:8; 17:24); the site is uncertain, so these coordinates are approximate.

locations.name: Brook Cherith
locations.modernName: Uncertain; Wadi Qelt (tradition) or Wadi Yabis (proposed)
locations.description: Brook "before Jordan" where Elijah hid and the ravens fed him (1 Kgs 17:3-5); the identification is uncertain, and Wadi Qelt near Jericho is the traditional choice, so these coordinates are approximate.

locations.name: Abel-meholah
locations.description: Hometown of Elisha son of Shaphat (1 Kgs 19:16); a Jordan Valley site south of Beth-shean, with Tell Abu Sifri and other tells proposed, so these coordinates are approximate.

locations.name: Shunem
locations.description: Town on the south side of the Jezreel Valley where the Shunammite woman hosted Elisha (2 Kgs 4:8), identified with modern Solem.

locations.name: Riblah
locations.description: Nebuchadnezzar's field headquarters on the Orontes, where Zedekiah was judged and Judah's leaders were put to death.

locations.name: Tahpanhes
locations.description: A fortress town on Egypt's eastern Delta frontier where the Judean remnant took Jeremiah after the murder of Gedaliah.

locations.name: River Ahava
locations.modernName: uncertain, a canal or stream in Babylonia
locations.description: The stream where Ezra mustered the returning exiles. The exact site is uncertain; Hit on the Euphrates, in the Babylonian homeland, is one proposal.

locations.name: Bethabara beyond Jordan
locations.description: Where John was baptizing (John 1:28). The King James text reads Bethabara; most Greek manuscripts read Bethany. The east-bank site of Al-Maghtas is the leading modern proposal; the exact place is uncertain.

locations.name: Sychar and Jacobs Well
locations.description: Where Jesus met the Samaritan woman at Jacobs well near the parcel of ground Jacob gave Joseph (John 4:5-6). The well beside Tell Balata is the long-standing identification; Sychar is usually placed at nearby Askar.

locations.name: Pool of Bethesda
locations.description: The pool by the sheep market with five porches where Jesus healed a man infirm 38 years (John 5:2-9). The twin pools north of the Temple Mount are the accepted site.

locations.name: Pool of Siloam
locations.description: Where the man born blind washed and received sight (John 9:7). The pool at the south end of the City of David, fed by Hezekiahs tunnel, is the traditional site; a larger Second Temple pool has been uncovered nearby.

locations.name: Ephraim
locations.description: The city near the wilderness where Jesus stayed with his disciples before the last Passover (John 11:54). Identification with et-Taiyiba, north-east of Jerusalem, is probable but not certain.

locations.name: Temple Mount
locations.description: Site of Herods temple with its courts and Solomons porch on the east side (John 10:23; Acts 3:11) and the Beautiful gate (Acts 3:2).

locations.name: Gethsemane
locations.modernName: Garden of Gethsemane, Mount of Olives
locations.description: The garden across the brook Cedron where Jesus went with his disciples and was arrested (John 18:1-12; Matt 26:36). The groves at the foot of the Mount of Olives are the traditional site.

locations.name: Golgotha
locations.modernName: Church of the Holy Sepulchre, Jerusalem
locations.description: The place of a skull outside the city wall, with a garden and a new tomb nearby (John 19:17, 41-42). Marked here at the ancient tradition under the Church of the Holy Sepulchre; the Garden Tomb, north of the Damascus Gate, is a nineteenth-century proposal.

locations.name: Lydda
locations.description: Town where Peter healed Aeneas, eaten with palsy eight years (Acts 9:32-35); near Joppa (Acts 9:38). Identified with modern Lod.

journeys.name: Book of Acts
journeys.description: The spread of the early church from Jerusalem to Rome, following the narrative of Acts.

stops.label: Pentecost in Jerusalem
stops.description: The Holy Spirit descends on the apostles; Peter preaches and 3,000 are baptized.

stops.label: Stoning of Stephen
stops.description: Stephen is stoned; persecution scatters believers beyond Jerusalem.

stops.label: Philip Preaches in Samaria
stops.description: Philip performs miracles in Samaria; Simon the sorcerer believes.

stops.label: Ethiopian Eunuch Baptized
stops.description: Philip meets an Ethiopian official on the Gaza road and baptizes him.

stops.label: Conversion of Saul
stops.description: Saul encounters Christ on the Damascus road; Ananias restores his sight.

stops.label: Peter Raises Tabitha in Joppa
stops.description: Peter raises the disciple Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead.

stops.label: Peter and Cornelius in Caesarea
stops.description: Peter receives a vision; the first Gentiles receive the Holy Spirit.

stops.label: Church Established in Antioch
stops.description: Believers first called "Christians" in Antioch; Barnabas and Saul teach.

stops.label: Barnabas and Saul in Cyprus
stops.description: Paul blinds the sorcerer Bar-Jesus; proconsul Sergius Paulus believes.

stops.label: Paul Preaches in Pisidian Antioch
stops.description: Paul's sermon in the synagogue; many believe but Jews stir up opposition.

stops.label: Iconium — Belief and Opposition
stops.description: Paul and Barnabas preach; the city divides; they flee before stoning.

stops.label: Lystra — Healing and Stoning
stops.description: Paul heals a lame man; mistaken for gods; then stoned and left for dead.

stops.label: Derbe — Many Disciples
stops.description: Paul and Barnabas make many disciples and begin the return journey.

stops.label: Council of Jerusalem
stops.description: Church leaders decide Gentiles need not be circumcised.

stops.label: Macedonian Vision at Troas
stops.description: Paul receives a vision: "Come over to Macedonia and help us."

stops.label: Lydia Converted in Philippi
stops.description: Lydia believes; Paul and Silas imprisoned; jailer converted.

stops.label: Paul in Thessalonica
stops.description: Paul reasons in the synagogue; accused of "turning the world upside down."

stops.label: Noble-Minded Bereans
stops.description: The Bereans examine the Scriptures daily to verify Paul's message.

stops.label: Paul on the Areopagus in Athens
stops.description: Paul preaches about the "Unknown God" on Mars Hill.

stops.label: Paul in Corinth — 18 Months
stops.description: Paul stays with Aquila and Priscilla; Gallio dismisses charges.

stops.label: Paul in Ephesus — 2 Years
stops.description: Extraordinary miracles; burning of occult scrolls; riot of Demetrius.

stops.label: Farewell to Ephesian Elders at Miletus
stops.description: Paul's emotional farewell: "I have not coveted anyone's silver or gold."

stops.label: Paul Arrested in Jerusalem
stops.description: Paul seized in the temple; transferred to Roman custody.

stops.label: Paul's Trial before Felix and Festus
stops.description: Paul held in Caesarea for two years; appeals to Caesar.

stops.label: Storm and Fair Havens of Crete
stops.description: Paul warns against sailing; a violent storm batters the ship 14 days.

stops.label: Shipwreck on Malta
stops.description: All 276 aboard survive; Paul bitten by a viper but unharmed; heals the sick.

stops.label: Landing at Puteoli
stops.description: Paul welcomed by believers at the Italian port.

stops.label: Paul Arrives in Rome
stops.description: Paul preaches the kingdom of God under house arrest for two years.

journeys.name: Book of Genesis
journeys.description: From Creation through the patriarchs — Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph — ending with Israel in Egypt.

stops.label: Creation
stops.description: God creates the heavens, the earth, and mankind in His image.

stops.label: The Fall
stops.description: Adam and Eve disobey God and are expelled from the Garden of Eden.

stops.label: The Flood
stops.description: God judges the earth with a flood; Noah and his family are saved on the ark.

stops.label: Tower of Babel
stops.description: Humanity is scattered when God confuses their language at the tower.

stops.label: Call of Abraham
stops.description: God appears to Abram in Mesopotamia before he settles in Haran (Acts 7:2-4) and tells him to leave for a land He will show him (Gen 12:1-3). Ussher dates his departure from Haran to 1921 BC.

stops.label: Abraham in Haran
stops.description: Abram settles in Haran with Terah; after Terah's death, he departs for Canaan.

stops.label: Abraham at Shechem
stops.description: Abram arrives in Canaan; God promises the land. Abraham builds an altar.

stops.label: Abram in Egypt
stops.description: Famine drives Abram to Egypt; Pharaoh takes Sarai but is plagued.

stops.label: Abrahamic Covenant at Hebron
stops.description: God makes a covenant with Abraham at the oaks of Mamre, promising countless descendants.

stops.label: Covenant of Circumcision
stops.description: God establishes circumcision as the sign of His covenant with Abraham.

stops.label: Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
stops.description: Abraham intercedes; God destroys the cities but Lot escapes.

stops.label: Hagar and Ishmael at Beersheba
stops.description: Hagar and Ishmael sent away; God provides a well in the wilderness.

stops.label: Binding of Isaac on Mount Moriah
stops.description: Abraham's faith tested; God provides a ram as a substitute.

stops.label: Isaac Settles at Beersheba
stops.description: Driven by famine and strife from Gerar, Isaac settles at Beersheba, where God renews the covenant and Abimelech makes peace with him. Jacob and Esau had been born twenty years after his marriage (Gen 25:19-26).

stops.label: Jacob's Dream at Bethel
stops.description: Fleeing Esau, Jacob dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven and God renews to him the promise made to Abraham.

stops.label: Jacob Flees to Haran
stops.description: Jacob leaves home, reaches Haran and serves Laban for twenty years, marrying Leah and Rachel (Gen 29-31).

stops.label: Jacob Wrestles God at Peniel
stops.description: Jacob wrestles with God and is renamed Israel.

stops.label: Jacob Returns to Shechem
stops.description: Jacob returns to Canaan and buys land at Shechem; Dinah incident.

stops.label: Jacob Returns to Hebron
stops.description: Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre (Hebron); Rachel has died near Bethlehem on the way (Gen 35:16-20). Isaac dies at 180 and is buried by his sons (Gen 35:28-29).

stops.label: Joseph Sold into Slavery
stops.description: Joseph's brothers sell him to traders headed for Egypt.

stops.label: Joseph Made Ruler of Egypt
stops.description: After interpreting Pharaoh's dreams, Joseph becomes second-in-command.

stops.label: Israel Enters Goshen
stops.description: Jacob's family (70 people) settles in Goshen at Pharaoh's invitation.

journeys.name: Book of Exodus
journeys.description: The deliverance of Israel from Egypt, through the wilderness to Mount Sinai and the building of the Tabernacle, then on to Kadesh Barnea and the Jordan.

stops.label: Israel Enslaved in Goshen
stops.description: A new Pharaoh arises who does not know Joseph; Israel is enslaved and multiplies.

stops.label: The Ten Plagues
stops.description: Moses confronts Pharaoh; God sends ten plagues upon Egypt, ending with the death of every firstborn.

stops.label: The Passover and Departure
stops.description: Israel keeps the first Passover and sets out from Rameses with great wealth.

stops.label: Crossing the Red Sea
stops.description: God parts the sea; Israel passes through on dry ground; Pharaoh's army is destroyed.

stops.label: Bitter Waters of Marah
stops.description: Israel's first crisis: bitter water is made sweet by a tree God shows Moses.

stops.label: Rest at Elim
stops.description: Israel camps at an oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees.

stops.label: Water from the Rock at Rephidim
stops.description: God provides water from a rock; Israel defeats Amalek while Moses' hands are raised.

stops.label: Giving of the Law at Sinai
stops.description: God descends on Mount Sinai in fire and thunder; gives the Ten Commandments and the Law.

stops.label: The Golden Calf
stops.description: While Moses is on the mountain, Aaron makes a golden calf; God's anger and Moses' intercession.

stops.label: The Tabernacle Completed
stops.description: Israel builds the Tabernacle according to God's pattern; the glory of the Lord fills it.

stops.label: Wilderness Wandering — Kadesh Barnea
stops.description: The twelve spies return; ten give a bad report. Israel is condemned to wander 40 years.

stops.label: Arrival at the Jordan
stops.description: After 40 years, the new generation reaches the Jordan River opposite the Promised Land.

journeys.name: Gospel of Luke
journeys.description: The life of Jesus from birth through resurrection, following Luke's orderly account.

stops.label: Zechariah in the Temple
stops.description: The angel Gabriel announces the birth of John the Baptist to the priest Zechariah.

stops.label: Annunciation in Nazareth
stops.description: Gabriel tells the virgin Mary she will bear the Son of God.

stops.label: Birth of Jesus in Bethlehem
stops.description: Jesus is born in a manger; angels announce the birth to shepherds.

stops.label: Presentation at the Temple
stops.description: Mary and Joseph present Jesus at the Temple; Simeon and Anna prophesy.

stops.label: The Boy Jesus in Nazareth
stops.description: Jesus grows up in Nazareth; at age 12 astounds the teachers in the Temple.

stops.label: Baptism of Jesus at the Jordan
stops.description: Jesus is baptized by John; the Holy Spirit descends; the Father speaks.

stops.label: Rejected at Nazareth
stops.description: Jesus reads Isaiah in the synagogue; his hometown tries to throw him off a cliff.

stops.label: Ministry Begins in Capernaum
stops.description: Jesus drives out a demon in the synagogue and heals Peter's mother-in-law.

stops.label: Great Catch of Fish
stops.description: Jesus calls Simon Peter, James, and John after a miraculous catch of fish.

stops.label: Raising the Widow's Son at Nain
stops.description: Jesus raises a widow's only son from the dead; "God has visited His people."

stops.label: Calming the Storm
stops.description: Jesus rebukes the wind and waves; the disciples ask, "Who is this?"

stops.label: Healing of the Gerasene Demoniac
stops.description: Jesus casts Legion out of a man among the tombs on the eastern shore; Matthew places it at Gadara, Mark and Luke at the country of the Gerasenes.

stops.label: Feeding of the 5,000 near Bethsaida
stops.description: Jesus feeds 5,000 men with five loaves and two fish.

stops.label: The Good Samaritan — Road to Jericho
stops.description: Jesus tells the parable of the Good Samaritan to a lawyer's question.

stops.label: Mary and Martha in Bethany
stops.description: Martha serves while Mary sits at Jesus' feet; "Mary has chosen the good portion."

stops.label: Healing of Blind Bartimaeus
stops.description: Jesus heals a blind man near Jericho; Zacchaeus believes.

stops.label: Crucifixion in Jerusalem
stops.description: Jesus is crucified at Golgotha; "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do."

stops.label: The Empty Tomb
stops.description: Women find the tomb empty; angels declare, "He is not here; He has risen!"

stops.label: Road to Emmaus
stops.description: The risen Jesus walks with two disciples; revealed in the breaking of bread.

stops.label: Ascension near Jerusalem
stops.description: Jesus blesses the disciples and is taken up into heaven near Bethany.

journeys.name: Book of Jonah
journeys.description: The prophet Jonah flees from God, is swallowed by a great fish, and ultimately preaches repentance to Nineveh.

stops.label: God's Call to Jonah
stops.description: The word of the Lord comes to Jonah (the text names no place; his home was Gath-hepher): "Go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry out against it."

stops.label: Jonah Flees to Joppa
stops.description: Instead of obeying, Jonah goes down to Joppa and boards a ship bound for Tarshish — away from God.

stops.label: The Great Storm at Sea
stops.description: God hurls a great wind; the sailors cast lots; Jonah confesses and is thrown overboard.

stops.label: Swallowed by the Great Fish
stops.description: God appoints a great fish to swallow Jonah. He prays from its belly for three days and nights.

stops.label: Jonah Preaches in Nineveh
stops.description: Jonah walks through the great city crying, "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!"

stops.label: Nineveh Repents
stops.description: The king and all the people repent in sackcloth and ashes; God relents from disaster.

stops.label: Jonah's Anger and the Vine
stops.description: Jonah is angry that God showed mercy. God teaches him compassion through a vine and a worm.

journeys.name: Into the Promised Land
journeys.description: From Kadesh through the last wilderness years, across the Jordan and through the conquest to the covenant at Shechem.

stops.label: Kadesh: Miriam Dies, Moses Strikes the Rock
stops.description: In the fortieth year Miriam dies at Kadesh, the people have no water, and Moses strikes the rock; Edom refuses them passage.

stops.label: Aaron Dies on Mount Hor
stops.description: Moses takes Aaron and Eleazar up the mountain, strips Aaron of the priestly garments and puts them on Eleazar; Aaron dies there.

stops.label: The Bronze Serpent
stops.description: Discouraged on the road around Edom, the people are bitten by fiery serpents; Moses lifts up a bronze serpent and all who look live.

stops.label: Plains of Moab: Balak and Balaam
stops.description: Israel camps on the plains of Moab; Balak hires Balaam, who can only bless Israel.

stops.label: Moses Views the Land from Nebo
stops.description: Moses climbs Mount Nebo, sees the land he will not enter, and dies there.

stops.label: Crossing the Jordan
stops.description: The priests carry the ark into the Jordan, the waters stand up, and Israel crosses on dry ground; twelve stones are set up.

stops.label: Gilgal: Circumcision and Passover
stops.description: At Gilgal the new generation is circumcised, keeps the Passover, eats the produce of the land, and the manna ceases.

stops.label: The Fall of Jericho
stops.description: Israel marches round the city for seven days and the wall falls; Rahab and her household are saved.

stops.label: Ai: Achan's Sin and Victory
stops.description: Israel is defeated at Ai because of Achan's theft; after Achan is judged, Joshua takes the city by ambush.

stops.label: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim
stops.description: Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal and reads the blessings and curses of the law to all Israel between Ebal and Gerizim.

stops.label: Gibeon: The Sun Stands Still
stops.description: Joshua defends the Gibeonites against five kings, and the sun and moon stand still while Israel wins the day.

stops.label: The Tabernacle Set Up at Shiloh
stops.description: The whole congregation gathers at Shiloh and sets up the tabernacle; the land is then surveyed and divided by lot.

stops.label: Shechem: Joshua's Covenant
stops.description: Joshua gathers the tribes, recounts God's dealings with them, and calls them to choose: 'as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.'

journeys.name: The Judges and Ruth
journeys.description: The deliverers raised up across the land, with Ruth's road from Moab to Bethlehem and Samuel's beginnings at Shiloh.

stops.label: Othniel Delivers Israel
stops.description: Othniel of Debir, who had taken the city and won Achsah as his wife (Judg 1:11-13), is raised up when Israel serves Cushan-rishathaim; the Spirit of the LORD comes on him and the land has rest forty years.

stops.label: Ehud Kills Eglon
stops.description: Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, brings tribute to Eglon of Moab at the city of palm trees and kills him; Israel then defeats Moab at the fords of the Jordan.

stops.label: Deborah and Barak at Tabor and the Kishon
stops.description: Deborah summons Barak to Mount Tabor; the LORD routs Sisera's chariots by the river Kishon, and Jael kills Sisera.

stops.label: Gideon Called at Ophrah
stops.description: The angel of the LORD calls Gideon from the winepress at Ophrah; he pulls down his father's altar of Baal.

stops.label: Gideon at the Spring of Harod
stops.description: Gideon's army is cut from thirty-two thousand to three hundred at the spring of Harod, and Midian is routed with trumpets and pitchers.

stops.label: Jephthah at Mizpah of Gilead
stops.description: Gilead recalls Jephthah, who makes his vow at Mizpah and defeats the Ammonites.

stops.label: Ruth Leaves Moab
stops.description: After the deaths of her husband and sons, Naomi returns toward Judah and Ruth clings to her: 'thy people shall be my people.'

stops.label: Ruth and Boaz at Bethlehem
stops.description: Ruth gleans in Boaz's field, Boaz redeems the family land and marries her, and their line leads to David.

stops.label: Samson Born at Zorah
stops.description: The angel announces a son to Manoah's wife; Samson is born a Nazirite and the Spirit begins to move him.

stops.label: Hannah's Prayer at Shiloh
stops.description: Barren Hannah prays at the house of the LORD in Shiloh, Eli blesses her, and she bears Samuel.

stops.label: The Call of Samuel at Shiloh
stops.description: The LORD calls the boy Samuel in the night and Eli hears the word of judgment on his house.

stops.label: Samson at Timnah
stops.description: Samson goes down to Timnah, takes a Philistine wife, kills a lion and poses his riddle.

stops.label: Samson at Gaza
stops.description: Samson carries off the gates of Gaza, and is later brought back there blind; he pulls down the temple of Dagon.

stops.label: Samuel Judges Israel at Mizpah
stops.description: Israel gathers at Mizpah, puts away its idols and fasts; the LORD thunders on the Philistines and Samuel sets up Ebenezer.

journeys.name: David: Shepherd to King
journeys.description: David is anointed in Bethlehem, faces Goliath, flees Saul, is made king at Hebron and Jerusalem, and returns from exile in Absalom's revolt.

stops.label: Samuel Anoints David
stops.description: Samuel comes to Jesse's house and, passing over the older sons, anoints the youngest, David, who is keeping the sheep.

stops.label: David and Goliath
stops.description: David, sent with food for his brothers, takes up Goliath's challenge and kills him with a sling and a stone.

stops.label: In Saul's Court at Gibeah
stops.description: David serves Saul and befriends Jonathan, but Saul's jealousy turns murderous and David escapes with the help of Michal and Jonathan.

stops.label: Bread at Nob
stops.description: Fleeing Saul, David receives holy bread and Goliath's sword from Ahimelech the priest at Nob.

stops.label: Feigning Madness at Gath
stops.description: David goes to Achish king of Gath, is recognised, and escapes by pretending to be mad.

stops.label: The Cave of Adullam
stops.description: David hides in the cave of Adullam, and his family and about four hundred distressed men gather to him.

stops.label: Rescuing Keilah
stops.description: David defeats the Philistines at Keilah, then learns that the town would hand him over to Saul and leaves.

stops.label: Sparing Saul at En-gedi
stops.description: David cuts off the corner of Saul's robe in a cave and refuses to harm the Lord's anointed.

stops.label: Ziklag
stops.description: Achish gives David Ziklag. After the Amalekites burn it and take the families, David pursues and recovers everything.

stops.label: Made King at Hebron
stops.description: After Saul's death David goes up to Hebron, and the men of Judah anoint him king over Judah.

stops.label: King over All Israel
stops.description: The tribes of Israel come to David at Hebron and anoint him king over all Israel.

stops.label: Jerusalem Taken
stops.description: David takes the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites and makes it the city of David.

stops.label: The Ark Comes to Jerusalem
stops.description: David brings the ark of God up to Jerusalem with rejoicing and sets it in a tent.

stops.label: Refuge at Mahanaim
stops.description: Driven from Jerusalem by Absalom's revolt, David crosses the Jordan to Mahanaim, where Joab leads his army to victory and Absalom dies.

stops.label: Return to Jerusalem
stops.description: Judah invites David back, he crosses the Jordan, and he comes again to his house in Jerusalem.

journeys.name: Elijah and Elisha
journeys.description: The prophets Elijah and Elisha, from the brook Cherith and Mount Carmel to the chariot of fire, and Elisha's ministry from Shunem to Damascus.

stops.label: Fed at the Brook Cherith
stops.description: After telling Ahab there will be no rain, Elijah hides by the brook Cherith and ravens bring him bread and meat.

stops.label: The Widow of Zarephath
stops.description: The brook dries up and Elijah goes to Zarephath, where the widow's flour and oil do not run out and her son is raised.

stops.label: Fire on Mount Carmel
stops.description: Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal; the fire of the Lord falls and the people turn back to Him.

stops.label: Racing Ahab to Jezreel
stops.description: Rain ends the drought, and Elijah runs ahead of Ahab's chariot to the entrance of Jezreel.

stops.label: The Juniper Tree
stops.description: Threatened by Jezebel, Elijah flees to Beersheba and then into the wilderness, where an angel feeds him under a juniper tree.

stops.label: The Still Small Voice at Horeb
stops.description: Elijah travels forty days to Horeb, the mount of God, and hears the Lord in a still small voice.

stops.label: Elisha Called at Abel-meholah
stops.description: Elijah finds Elisha ploughing, throws his mantle over him, and Elisha leaves the oxen to follow him.

stops.label: Naboth's Vineyard
stops.description: Jezebel has Naboth killed so Ahab can take his vineyard at Jezreel, and Elijah pronounces judgment on Ahab and Jezebel.

stops.label: Bethel
stops.description: Elijah and Elisha come down from Gilgal to Bethel, and Elisha refuses to leave his master.

stops.label: Jericho
stops.description: At Jericho the sons of the prophets tell Elisha that his master will be taken, and the two go on towards the Jordan.

stops.label: The Chariot of Fire
stops.description: Elijah parts the Jordan and is taken up in a whirlwind by a chariot of fire; Elisha takes up his mantle and parts the river again.

stops.label: The Shunammite's Son
stops.description: At Shunem Elisha is hosted by a woman whose son he later raises from the dead.

stops.label: Naaman Healed in the Jordan
stops.description: Naaman, the Aramean commander, washes seven times in the Jordan and is cleansed, while Gehazi's greed brings leprosy on himself.

stops.label: The Army at Dothan
stops.description: The king of Aram sends an army to seize Elisha at Dothan, and the Lord opens the eyes of Elisha's servant to see the horses and chariots of fire.

stops.label: Samaria Besieged
stops.description: Ben-hadad besieges Samaria and famine grips the city, until the Lord scatters the Arameans and the people feast on their camp.

stops.label: Hazael at Damascus
stops.description: Elisha comes to Damascus and foretells that Hazael will be king of Aram; Hazael takes the throne.

journeys.name: Exile and Return
journeys.description: Judah is carried away to Babylon, lives and witnesses there, and comes home in waves under Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah to rebuild the Temple and the walls.

stops.label: Daniel Taken from Jerusalem
stops.description: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem and carries off vessels of the Temple and young nobles of Judah, among them Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, to be trained in Babylon.

stops.label: Jehoiachin Carried Away
stops.description: Nebuchadnezzar's army returns to the city; King Jehoiachin, the court, the craftsmen and ten thousand captives are taken to Babylon.

stops.label: Ezekiel by the Chebar
stops.description: Among the exiles on the river Chebar, the priest Ezekiel sees the heavens opened and the glory of God above the living creatures.

stops.label: Jerusalem Falls
stops.description: After a siege of about a year and a half the wall is breached; the Temple and the city are burned, the walls thrown down and the people carried away.

stops.label: Zedekiah Judged at Riblah
stops.description: Caught on the plains of Jericho, Zedekiah is brought to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, where his sons are killed before his eyes and he is blinded and bound for Babylon.

stops.label: Jeremiah and the Remnant at Tahpanhes
stops.description: Against Jeremiah's warning, the captains lead the remnant into Egypt, taking the prophet and Baruch with them as far as Tahpanhes.

stops.label: The Fiery Furnace
stops.description: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and are cast into the furnace; a fourth figure walks with them and they come out unharmed.

stops.label: Belshazzar's Feast
stops.description: A hand writes on the wall during Belshazzar's feast; Daniel reads it, and that night Babylon is taken and Darius the Median receives the kingdom.

stops.label: Daniel in the Lions' Den
stops.description: Daniel is thrown to the lions for praying to his God and is found unharmed in the morning.

stops.label: Cyrus Frees the Exiles
stops.description: Cyrus decrees that the Temple be rebuilt; Zerubbabel and Jeshua lead the first company of about forty-two thousand home to Judah.

stops.label: The Temple Finished
stops.description: After delays and the prophets' urging, the Temple is completed and dedicated, and the Passover is kept.

stops.label: Esther at Susa
stops.description: Esther, made queen of Persia, and her cousin Mordecai turn Haman's decree against the Jews, and Purim is established.

stops.label: Ezra Gathers the Exiles at the Ahava
stops.description: Ezra musters the returning company by the river Ahava, finds no Levites among them, sends for some, and the people fast and pray for a safe way.

stops.label: Ezra Arrives in Jerusalem
stops.description: After a journey of four months Ezra reaches Jerusalem with the king's gifts and the Temple vessels, which are weighed into the Temple.

stops.label: Nehemiah's Prayer at Susa
stops.description: Hearing that Jerusalem's walls are broken, the king's cupbearer Nehemiah prays, and Artaxerxes sends him to Judah as governor.

stops.label: Nehemiah Rebuilds the Walls
stops.description: Nehemiah surveys the ruined wall by night, the people build despite opposition, and the wall is finished in fifty-two days.

journeys.name: Jesus in John's Gospel
journeys.description: Jesus' ministry as John tells it: from the Jordan to Cana, the feasts at Jerusalem, Lazarus, the Passion and the breakfast by the Sea of Tiberias.

stops.label: Bethabara beyond Jordan
stops.description: John bears witness to Jesus where he is baptizing beyond the Jordan; Jesus is baptized and John points him out as the Lamb of God.

stops.label: Wedding at Cana
stops.description: At a marriage in Cana of Galilee Jesus turns water into wine, the beginning of his miracles.

stops.label: Capernaum
stops.description: Jesus goes down to Capernaum with his mother, his brethren and his disciples and stays a few days.

stops.label: Temple Cleansed at the First Passover
stops.description: At the Passover Jesus drives the merchants and moneychangers from the temple and speaks of raising up the temple of his body.

stops.label: Jacobs Well at Sychar
stops.description: Passing through Samaria, Jesus talks with a woman of Sychar at Jacobs well, and many Samaritans believe.

stops.label: The Officials Son
stops.description: Back in Cana, Jesus tells a nobleman of Capernaum that his son lives, and the man believes.

stops.label: Pool of Bethesda
stops.description: At a feast of the Jews Jesus heals a man who had been infirm 38 years and teaches on the authority of the Son.

stops.label: Five Thousand Fed by the Sea of Tiberias
stops.description: Jesus feeds a great crowd from five loaves and two fishes, walks on the sea and teaches on the bread of life.

stops.label: Feast of Tabernacles in Jerusalem
stops.description: Jesus goes up to the feast in the middle of it and teaches in the temple about living water and the light of the world.

stops.label: Pool of Siloam
stops.description: Jesus gives sight to a man born blind and sends him to wash in the pool of Siloam.

stops.label: Solomons Porch at the Feast of Dedication
stops.description: In winter Jesus walks in Solomons porch and tells the Jews, I and my Father are one.

stops.label: Lazarus Raised at Bethany
stops.description: Jesus comes to Bethany, weeps with Mary and Martha, and calls Lazarus out of the tomb.

stops.label: Ephraim
stops.description: After the plot against him Jesus withdraws to Ephraim near the wilderness with his disciples.

stops.label: Anointing at Bethany
stops.description: Six days before the Passover Mary anoints Jesus feet at supper while Lazarus sits at the table.

stops.label: Entry into Jerusalem
stops.description: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a young ass as the crowd cries Hosanna.

stops.label: The Upper Room
stops.description: At supper Jesus washes the disciples feet, speaks of the Comforter and prays for them.

stops.label: Gethsemane
stops.description: Jesus goes over the brook Cedron into a garden where Judas leads the officers to arrest him.

stops.label: Golgotha
stops.description: Jesus is crucified at the place of a skull and dies after saying, It is finished.

stops.label: The Tomb
stops.description: Joseph and Nicodemus bury Jesus in the garden tomb; on the first day Mary Magdalene finds it empty and sees the risen Lord.

stops.label: Breakfast by the Sea of Tiberias
stops.description: Jesus shows himself to seven disciples after a night of fishing and feeds them on the shore.

journeys.name: Peter
journeys.description: Simon Peter after the Ascension: Pentecost, Jerusalem, Samaria, the coast, Cornelius, prison and the council, ending at Antioch.

stops.label: Pentecost in Jerusalem
stops.description: The Spirit falls on the disciples; Peter stands up with the eleven and preaches, and about three thousand are added.

stops.label: The Lame Man at the Beautiful Gate
stops.description: Peter and John heal a man lame from birth at the temple gate and Peter preaches in Solomons porch.

stops.label: Before the Council
stops.description: Peter and John, and later all the apostles, answer the rulers: We ought to obey God rather than men.

stops.label: Samaria with John
stops.description: Peter and John come down from Jerusalem, pray for the Samaritans to receive the Holy Ghost, and rebuke Simon the sorcerer.

stops.label: Lydda and Aeneas
stops.description: Passing through the quarters, Peter heals Aeneas, who had kept his bed eight years with palsy.

stops.label: Joppa and Tabitha
stops.description: Called from Lydda, Peter prays and raises Tabitha (Dorcas) and stays many days with Simon a tanner.

stops.label: Caesarea and Cornelius
stops.description: Taught by a vision at Joppa, Peter goes to the centurion Cornelius, preaches, and the Holy Ghost falls on the Gentiles.

stops.label: Prison and Release in Jerusalem
stops.description: Herod Agrippa I has Peter imprisoned; an angel frees him and he goes to the house of Mary, mother of John Mark.

stops.label: Council in Jerusalem
stops.description: Peter rises at the council and testifies that Gentiles are saved by grace, as Jews are.

stops.label: Antioch
stops.description: Paul withstands Peter to the face at Antioch for drawing back from eating with Gentiles. Scripture ends Peters story here; tradition says he died at Rome under Nero (see Martyrdom of Peter and Paul, AD 67).
